questions.stem: A 17-year-old girl is worried because her menstrual cycles occur every 26 days while her friend's occur every 35 days. She asks whether either cycle length is abnormal. Menstrual cycle length is typically within which of the following ranges?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 10 to 20 days

choices.label: B
choices.text: 18 to 22 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: 24 to 38 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: 40 to 55 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: 56 to 70 days

explanation.summary: Menstrual cycles typically range from 24 to 38 days.
explanation.whyCorrect: Between menarche and menopause, cyclical ovarian production of estrogen and progesterone regulates menstrual cycles, which typically range from 24 to 38 days. Both a 26-day and a 35-day cycle fall within this typical range.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 10- to 20-day range lies entirely below the typical span and would exclude both normal cycles described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An 18- to 22-day range falls short of the typical lower limit of 24 days.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cycles of 40 to 55 days exceed the typical upper limit of 38 days.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cycles of 56 to 70 days are far beyond the typical range.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with regular cycles is evaluated on day 22, about one week after ovulation. The follicle that released her oocyte has ruptured, yet her serum estrogen level remains substantial. Which of the following is the principal source of this estrogen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The dominant preovulatory follicle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Primordial follicles in the ovarian cortex

choices.label: C
choices.text: The anterior pituitary gland

choices.label: D
choices.text: The corpus luteum

choices.label: E
choices.text: The endometrial glands

explanation.summary: After follicle rupture, the luteinized follicular cells form the corpus luteum, which continues to synthesize estrogen during the luteal phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once the follicle ruptures and releases the secondary oocyte, the remaining follicular cells luteinize to form the corpus luteum. The corpus luteum continues to synthesize estrogen, in addition to large amounts of progesterone, throughout the luteal phase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The dominant follicle ruptured at ovulation a week earlier; it no longer exists as an intact estrogen-producing follicle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Primordial follicles are not the cyclic estrogen source; granulosa cells of developing follicles and then the corpus luteum are.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The anterior pituitary secretes LH and FSH; it does not synthesize estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The endometrium is a target of estrogen and progesterone, not a source of ovarian steroids.

questions.stem: In a study of peripheral estrogen metabolism, investigators observe that estrone and 17beta-estradiol can each be converted into the other. Which of the following enzymes catalyzes this interconversion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aromatase (CYP19A1 enzyme complex)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Desmolase, the side-chain cleavage enzyme

choices.label: C
choices.text: 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase

choices.label: D
choices.text: 21-hydroxylase of the adrenal cortex

choices.label: E
choices.text: 5-alpha-reductase type 2 isoenzyme

explanation.summary: 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase enzymes interconvert estrone (E1) and 17beta-estradiol (E2).
explanation.whyCorrect: In extragonadal tissues, aromatase generates estrone from androstenedione and 17beta-estradiol from testosterone. Estrone and estradiol can then be interconverted by 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase enzymes, linking the two estrogens metabolically.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aromatase converts androgens into estrogens; it does not interconvert the two estrogens.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Desmolase acts at the start of steroidogenesis, converting cholesterol to pregnenolone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 21-hydroxylase belongs to adrenal corticosteroid synthesis, not estrogen interconversion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 5-alpha-reductase converts testosterone to a more potent androgen and does not act on estrone or estradiol.

questions.stem: Radiolabeled testosterone is administered to a healthy volunteer and tracked into adipose tissue, where aromatase converts it to a labeled estrogen. Which of the following is the product of this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 17beta-estradiol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estrone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Androstenedione

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pregnenolone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Progesterone

explanation.summary: In extragonadal tissues, aromatase converts testosterone to 17beta-estradiol (E2) and androstenedione to estrone (E1).
explanation.whyCorrect: Aromatase expressed in extragonadal tissues such as adipose tissue converts specific androgen substrates to specific estrogens: androstenedione becomes estrone (E1), while testosterone becomes 17beta-estradiol (E2). With testosterone as the labeled substrate, the product is 17beta-estradiol.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Estrone is the aromatase product of androstenedione, not of testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Androstenedione is an androgen precursor upstream of aromatization, not an aromatase product of testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pregnenolone is formed from cholesterol by desmolase early in steroidogenesis, not by aromatase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progesterone is a progestogen synthesized by luteal cells; aromatase does not produce it from testosterone.

questions.stem: A physiologist traces gonadotropin-releasing hormone from its site of release in the hypothalamus to its receptors on gonadotrophs. By which of the following routes does GnRH reach the anterior pituitary gland?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Axonal transport to the posterior pituitary with systemic release

choices.label: B
choices.text: Release into the hypophyseal-portal vasculature to the anterior pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Diffusion through the cerebrospinal fluid to the pituitary surface

choices.label: D
choices.text: Systemic arterial circulation after passage through the liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Retrograde transport along the optic tracts to the sella turcica

explanation.summary: GnRH is released from the hypothalamus into the hypophyseal-portal vasculature and then binds receptors on the anterior pituitary.
explanation.whyCorrect: GnRH is released from the hypothalamus into the hypophyseal-portal vasculature, a dedicated vascular route to the anterior pituitary gland. There it binds its receptors on the anterior pituitary, causing release of LH and FSH.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GnRH acts on the anterior pituitary via portal blood, not by axonal delivery to the posterior pituitary.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GnRH travels in the portal vessels, not by diffusion through cerebrospinal fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GnRH does not need to traverse the systemic circulation or liver; the portal route carries it directly to the anterior pituitary.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There is no optic-tract transport route for GnRH; delivery is vascular via the portal system.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with regular 28-day cycles is studied on cycle day 21. Serum estradiol and progesterone are both elevated, and serum LH and FSH are low. Which of the following best explains the low gonadotropin levels?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Positive feedback by sustained high estradiol on the anterior pituitary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Downregulation of GnRH receptors caused by continuous GnRH exposure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Selective negative feedback on LH secretion by granulosa-cell inhibin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Negative feedback by estradiol and progesterone on GnRH, LH, and FSH release

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppression of gonadotrophs by embryo-derived human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation.summary: Ovarian estradiol and progesterone feed back negatively to reduce GnRH, LH, and FSH release.
explanation.whyCorrect: Like most hormones, GnRH, LH, and FSH undergo negative feedback. Estradiol and progesterone produced when LH and FSH act on the ovary feed back to reduce GnRH, LH, and FSH release, and progesterone's functions include decreasing gonadotropin secretion, which helps regulate ovarian cycles. High luteal-phase steroid levels therefore suppress LH and FSH.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Positive feedback by sustained high estradiol occurs near the end of the follicular phase and produces an LH surge, not low gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH receptor downregulation follows continuous GnRH administration; normal physiology uses pulsatile GnRH release.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin selectively decreases FSH secretion, not LH, and does not account for suppression of both gonadotropins by luteal steroids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG is produced by an early embryo after implantation; there is no indication of pregnancy in a routine day-21 study.

questions.stem: Early in the follicular phase, FSH must rise enough to recruit and support developing follicles, and later its concentration must fall enough to stop the growth of less-responsive follicles so that a single dominant follicle matures. Which of the following pairs of hormones balances FSH availability in this way?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activin and inhibin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estradiol and progesterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: LH and human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: D
choices.text: GnRH and progesterone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Estradiol and human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation.summary: Activin promotes FSH synthesis and secretion while inhibin suppresses it; together they set FSH so one dominant follicle matures.
explanation.whyCorrect: Activin, produced within both the ovary and anterior pituitary, promotes FSH synthesis and secretion, whereas granulosa-cell inhibin selectively decreases FSH secretion. Together they regulate FSH so that enough is available to recruit developing follicles but the level subsequently falls enough to stop less-responsive follicles, normally allowing a single dominant follicle to mature and ovulate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Estradiol and progesterone provide negative feedback on gonadotropins broadly; neither promotes FSH synthesis to support recruitment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LH is itself a gonadotropin and hCG is an embryonic pregnancy signal; neither constitutes the push-pull control of FSH.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GnRH stimulates both gonadotropins and progesterone suppresses them; this pair does not include a selective FSH promoter and inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG rescues the corpus luteum in pregnancy and estradiol suppresses gonadotropins during most of the follicular phase; neither promotes FSH synthesis.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman with regular cycles does not conceive during the current cycle. On the first day of her menstrual period, her endometrial lining begins to break down. Which of the following hormonal events directly precipitates this breakdown?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A rise in hCG secreted by an implanted embryo

choices.label: B
choices.text: A midcycle surge of LH from the anterior pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: A sustained rise in estradiol from the dominant follicle

choices.label: D
choices.text: A fall in FSH caused by granulosa-cell inhibin

choices.label: E
choices.text: A fall in progesterone as the corpus luteum degenerates

explanation.summary: Without fertilization and implantation, the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone falls, and the endometrial lining breaks down.
explanation.whyCorrect: If fertilization and implantation do not occur, the corpus luteum gradually degenerates. Progesterone levels then decrease, and because progesterone maintains the uterine endometrial lining, the endometrium breaks down and the menstrual cycle begins again.

whyWrongByChoice.A: hCG appears only when an embryo implants; it prevents luteal involution and would preserve, not shed, the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The LH surge occurs at midcycle and triggers ovulation; it does not cause endometrial breakdown two weeks later.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sustained high estradiol produces the preovulatory LH surge; estradiol stimulates endometrial proliferation rather than breakdown.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin's selective suppression of FSH restricts follicle maturation; it does not control endometrial shedding.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with cirrhosis has reduced levels of the plasma proteins that transport sex steroids, increasing the free fraction of these lipid-soluble hormones. Which of the following organs normally synthesizes albumin, sex hormone-binding globulin, and corticosteroid-binding globulin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ovary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anterior pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Liver

choices.label: D
choices.text: Adrenal cortex

choices.label: E
choices.text: Kidney

explanation.summary: The carrier proteins for estrogens and progesterone — albumin, SHBG, and CBG — are made in the liver.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogens circulate primarily bound to albumin and sex hormone-binding globulin, and progesterone circulates primarily bound to albumin and corticosteroid-binding globulin. These transport proteins are made in the liver, so hepatic disease reduces their production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The ovary synthesizes the steroid hormones themselves, not their plasma carrier proteins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The anterior pituitary secretes LH and FSH; it does not produce plasma binding proteins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The adrenal cortex makes steroid hormones, not the globulins that carry them.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The kidney is not the source of albumin or the hormone-binding globulins.

questions.stem: A researcher fractionates estrogen-responsive cells to map the subcellular distribution of estrogen receptors. In which of the following locations are estrogen receptors primarily found?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Plasma membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nucleus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitochondria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lysosomes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rough endoplasmic reticulum

explanation.summary: Estrogen receptors are located primarily in the nucleus, with additional populations in the cytoplasm and at the plasma membrane.
explanation.whyCorrect: After estrogen dissociates from its plasma-binding protein, it diffuses directly across the plasma membrane. Its receptors are located primarily in the nucleus, with additional receptor populations in the cytoplasm and associated with the plasma membrane, so the nucleus is where most receptors are found.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A membrane-associated receptor population exists, but it is not the primary location of estrogen receptors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mitochondria are not described as a site of estrogen receptors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lysosomes are degradative organelles, not estrogen receptor locations.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The rough endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes proteins but is not where estrogen receptors reside.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman is diagnosed with estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, in which hormone binding signals the tumor cells to divide. Her oncologist prescribes tamoxifen. Which of the following best describes how this medication helps treat her cancer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It inhibits aromatase in adipose and other peripheral tissues

choices.label: B
choices.text: It blocks desmolase from converting cholesterol to pregnenolone

choices.label: C
choices.text: It selectively lowers FSH secretion in the manner of inhibin

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reduces signaling through estrogen receptors in the tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: It halts hepatic production of sex hormone-binding globulin

explanation.summary: Tamoxifen reduces estrogen-receptor signaling in estrogen receptor-positive breast cancers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some breast cancers are estrogen receptor positive, meaning their receptors signal the cell to divide when bound by hormone, just as in many normal cells. Hormone receptor status guides treatment, and tamoxifen reduces estrogen-receptor signaling in estrogen receptor-positive breast cancers, decreasing the proliferative signal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Decreasing peripheral estrogen synthesis by inhibiting aromatase is the mechanism of aromatase inhibitors, not tamoxifen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Desmolase acts at the first step of ovarian steroidogenesis; tamoxifen does not target this enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin-like suppression of FSH is a feedback mechanism at the pituitary, not tamoxifen's action on the tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tamoxifen works at the estrogen receptor; it does not act by eliminating hepatic binding-protein synthesis.

questions.stem: In an experiment, uterine tissue from an animal deprived of ovarian hormones responds only weakly to administered progesterone. Pretreating the animal with 17beta-estradiol for several days markedly enhances the uterine response to the same dose of progesterone. Which of the following best explains this observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estradiol induces expression of progesterone receptors in the uterus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estradiol is converted to progesterone within the uterine cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol displaces progesterone from corticosteroid-binding globulin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estradiol blocks hepatic degradation of circulating progesterone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Estradiol converts uterine progesterone to a more potent metabolite

explanation.summary: One of estrogen's functions is inducing progesterone receptors in tissues such as the uterus, breast, and brain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among its key functions, estrogen induces progesterone receptors in several tissues, including the uterus, breast, and brain. Estradiol pretreatment therefore increases the number of progesterone receptors in the uterus, so the same dose of progesterone produces a much larger response.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Estradiol is an end-product estrogen; it is not converted into progesterone in target tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Displacement from a plasma carrier is not the described mechanism; the enhancement occurs at the level of tissue receptors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture attributes the priming effect to receptor induction, not to altered hormone degradation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progesterone itself is the active progestogen; estradiol does not act by generating a more potent progesterone metabolite.

questions.stem: A study compares serum lipoprotein profiles of premenopausal women with high endogenous estradiol levels to those of estradiol-deficient women. Which of the following lipoprotein patterns is expected in the women with high estradiol?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased LDL cholesterol and decreased HDL cholesterol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased HDL cholesterol and decreased LDL cholesterol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased HDL cholesterol and increased LDL cholesterol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decreased HDL cholesterol and decreased LDL cholesterol

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unchanged HDL cholesterol and unchanged LDL cholesterol

explanation.summary: Estrogen increases HDL cholesterol and decreases LDL cholesterol.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among its functions beyond the reproductive tract, estrogen increases high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol and decreases low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol. Women with high estradiol therefore show higher HDL and lower LDL than estradiol-deficient women.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is the reverse of estrogen's effect on the lipoprotein profile.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estrogen lowers LDL; it does not raise both lipoprotein fractions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Estrogen raises HDL; it does not lower both fractions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estrogen actively changes the lipoprotein profile rather than leaving it unchanged.

questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl in mid-puberty has developing breasts and an emerging female pattern of fat distribution. Which of the following hormones is primarily responsible for the development of these female secondary sex characteristics?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Progesterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

choices.label: C
choices.text: 17beta-estradiol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Follicle-stimulating hormone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibin

explanation.summary: Estrogen develops and maintains female secondary sex characteristics after puberty, including breast development and female fat distribution.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogen has major roles in the development and maintenance of the female reproductive tract and secondary sex characteristics. Developing and maintaining female secondary characteristics after puberty — breast development and female fat distribution — is among its listed functions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Progesterone contributes to breast development through fat cell growth and alveolar-lobular development, but the paired secondary sex characteristics of breast development and female fat distribution are attributed to estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: LH stimulates theca cells in steroid synthesis; it is not the hormone that directly produces secondary sex characteristics.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FSH induces granulosa-cell aromatase; the downstream estrogen, not FSH itself, drives the secondary sex characteristics.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibin selectively suppresses FSH secretion and has no role in secondary sex characteristics.

questions.stem: A physiologist lists the actions of the ovarian steroid hormones on their target tissues. Which of the following actions is a function of progesterone rather than estrogen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stimulating proliferation of the endometrium before ovulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Promoting growth and maintenance of the breast ductal system

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increasing HDL cholesterol and decreasing LDL cholesterol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Triggering the LH surge that is essential for ovulation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inducing fat cell growth and alveolar-lobular development in the breast

explanation.summary: Progesterone develops the breasts by inducing fat cell growth and division and alveolar-lobular development; estrogen handles the ductal system.
explanation.whyCorrect: Progesterone prepares the breasts for lactation by inducing fat cell growth and division as well as alveolar-lobular development. Estrogen, by contrast, promotes growth and maintenance of the breast ductal system, so the two hormones develop different components of the breast.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stimulating endometrial proliferation before ovulation is an estrogen function; progesterone instead differentiates the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Growth and maintenance of the breast ductal system is listed under estrogen's preparation of the breasts for pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The favorable lipoprotein changes — higher HDL and lower LDL — are effects of estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Triggering the LH surge essential for ovulation is an estrogen function via positive feedback.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman in the luteal phase of her cycle is noted to have thick cervical mucus that limits sperm penetration and helps reduce the entry of ascending microbes into the upper reproductive tract. Which of the following hormones produces this change in the mucus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Progesterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: 17beta-estradiol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Follicle-stimulating hormone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Activin

explanation.summary: Progesterone thickens cervical mucus, limiting sperm penetration and helping reduce ascending microbial entry.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among progesterone's functions is thickening cervical mucus, which limits sperm penetration and helps reduce ascending microbial entry. In the luteal phase, the corpus luteum synthesizes large amounts of progesterone, accounting for the thick mucus observed.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Estradiol's listed reproductive-tract actions include endometrial proliferation and tract maintenance, not luteal-phase thickening of cervical mucus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSH acts on granulosa cells to induce aromatase; it does not act on cervical mucus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LH stimulates theca cells and triggers ovulation; it does not thicken cervical mucus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Activin promotes FSH synthesis and secretion and has no described action on cervical mucus.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with chronic anovulation undergoes endometrial biopsy, which shows excessive endometrial growth consistent with endometrial hyperplasia. Her serum estradiol has been within the normal range. Which of the following best explains the excessive growth of her endometrium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Loss of estrogen receptor expression in the endometrial glands

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of progesterone because no corpus luteum forms

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess inhibin secretion by ovarian granulosa cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sustained hCG production by the endometrial stroma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Persistent progesterone secretion by a retained corpus luteum

explanation.summary: Progesterone maintains a healthy uterine lining by preventing excessive growth; without ovulation there is no corpus luteum and no progesterone to restrain estrogen-driven proliferation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among progesterone's functions is maintaining a healthy uterine lining and preventing excessive growth that could lead to endometrial hyperplasia. Because the corpus luteum forms from luteinized follicular cells only after ovulation, chronic anovulation leaves the estrogen-stimulated endometrium proliferating without progesterone's restraint, producing hyperplasia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Her endometrium is overgrowing in response to estrogen, which requires intact estrogen receptor signaling, not its loss.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin acts at the anterior pituitary to lower FSH; it does not regulate endometrial growth directly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hCG comes from an early embryo after implantation, not from the endometrium, and is not present here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Persistent progesterone would differentiate and restrain the endometrium — the opposite of unchecked proliferation.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with a 28-day cycle undergoes endometrial biopsy on day 23. The specimen shows a secretory endometrium of the type required for implantation of an embryo. Which of the following hormones induced this differentiation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 17beta-estradiol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Follicle-stimulating hormone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progesterone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

explanation.summary: Progesterone induces differentiation of the endometrium into the secretory endometrium required for implantation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogen stimulates endometrial proliferation before ovulation, but after ovulation progesterone from the corpus luteum induces differentiation of the endometrium into the secretory endometrium required for implantation, and it maintains the endometrium if pregnancy occurs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estradiol drives proliferation of the endometrium before ovulation; the secretory transformation is progesterone's role.
whyWrongByChoice.B: FSH acts on granulosa cells in the ovary and has no direct differentiating action on the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG appears only after implantation, where it preserves the corpus luteum; it does not create the secretory endometrium beforehand.
whyWrongByChoice.E: LH stimulates ovarian theca cells and triggers ovulation; it does not act on the endometrium to induce secretory change.

questions.stem: Following ovulation, the corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone along with estrogen. Which of the following best describes the cellular basis of this steroid production?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Luteinized granulosa cells alone supply every required synthetic enzyme

choices.label: B
choices.text: Luteinized theca cells alone supply every required synthetic enzyme

choices.label: C
choices.text: Luteinized theca and granulosa cells contribute different enzymes to synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Residual cumulus cells around the released oocyte perform all synthetic steps

choices.label: E
choices.text: Newly recruited primordial follicles supply the steroid precursors to luteal cells

explanation.summary: Luteal steroid synthesis depends on luteinized theca and granulosa cells, which contribute different enzymes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once the follicle ruptures and releases the egg, the theca and granulosa cells remaining in the ovary transform into luteal cells that synthesize large amounts of progesterone as well as estrogen. Luteinized theca and granulosa cells contribute different enzymes to steroid hormone synthesis, so the corpus luteum's output reflects the cooperation of both cell types.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Granulosa-derived luteal cells do not act alone; luteinized theca cells contribute distinct enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Theca-derived luteal cells likewise lack the full enzyme set; both luteinized cell types participate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The oocyte and its surrounding cells leave the follicle at ovulation; luteal steroids come from the cells remaining in the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primordial follicles are not a precursor source for the corpus luteum; cholesterol-based synthesis occurs within the luteal cells.

questions.stem: Radiolabeled LH and radiolabeled FSH are perfused over a developing ovarian follicle, and the binding sites of each gonadotropin are mapped. Which of the following distributions of receptor binding is expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: LH receptors on theca cells and FSH receptors on granulosa cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: FSH receptors on theca cells and LH receptors on granulosa cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receptors for both gonadotropins restricted to theca cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Receptors for both gonadotropins restricted to granulosa cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Receptors for both gonadotropins located on the oocyte itself

explanation.summary: LH binds its receptor on theca cells and FSH binds its receptor on granulosa cells in the two-cell model of estrogen synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In gonadal estrogen synthesis, LH released from the anterior pituitary binds to its receptor on a theca cell, driving the desmolase pathway toward androstenedione. FSH binds to its receptor on the granulosa cell, inducing aromatase to convert theca-derived androstenedione to 17beta-estradiol.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This reverses the arrangement: FSH receptors are on granulosa cells, not theca cells, and LH receptors are on theca cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Restricting both receptors to theca cells would leave no FSH-driven aromatase induction in granulosa cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Restricting both receptors to granulosa cells would leave no LH-stimulated androgen production in theca cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The oocyte is not the gonadotropin target; the surrounding theca and granulosa cells carry the receptors.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman has had no menstrual periods for the past 14 months, and her estrogen levels are markedly decreased. Which of the following best explains the loss of her cyclic ovarian activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Destruction of anterior pituitary gonadotrophs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Downregulation of GnRH receptors by continuous GnRH release

choices.label: C
choices.text: Persistence of a corpus luteum from a prior cycle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excess inhibin secretion from granulosa cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Depletion of the ovarian follicle pool

explanation.summary: Menopause results from depletion of the ovarian follicle pool, causing loss of ovarian cyclic activity, usually around 50-60 years of age.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogen levels decrease significantly at menopause, when depletion of the ovarian follicle pool results in loss of ovarian cyclic activity, usually around 50-60 years of age. Without follicles, cyclic granulosa-cell estrogen production ends, and low estrogen can cause problems such as diminished bone mass.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Menopause is an ovarian process of follicle depletion, not a destructive lesion of pituitary gonadotrophs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH receptor downregulation occurs with continuous exogenous GnRH exposure, not as the mechanism of natural menopause.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A corpus luteum degenerates when there is no pregnancy; a persistent one is not the cause of menopause.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin selectively suppresses FSH during follicle selection; excess inhibin is not the described cause of menopause.

questions.stem: In a longitudinal study, a woman's GnRH pulse frequency is observed to change with her environment, her age, and the time of the month. Which of the following properties of the hypothalamus makes this variability in pulse frequency possible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It secretes GnRH directly into the systemic arterial circulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: It stores GnRH within the posterior pituitary for reflex release

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its GnRH-producing neurons reside inside the anterior pituitary

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is connected to many other brain areas and receives inputs from many sources

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its GnRH output is determined entirely by circulating ovarian steroid levels

explanation.summary: GnRH pulse frequency can respond to environment, age, and time of the month because the hypothalamus is connected to many brain areas and receives inputs from many sources.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pulsatile release of GnRH by the hypothalamus is the basis for all reproductive hormone changes, and the pulse frequency changes with factors including environment, age, and time of the month. This is possible because the hypothalamus is connected to many other brain areas and is subject to inputs from many sources.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GnRH is released into the hypophyseal-portal vasculature to reach the anterior pituitary, not into the systemic arterial circulation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH is not a stored posterior pituitary hormone; it travels via portal blood to anterior pituitary receptors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GnRH neurons are hypothalamic; the anterior pituitary contains the gonadotrophs that respond to GnRH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ovarian steroid feedback is one influence, but the pulse frequency also responds to environment and age through broad neural inputs, so it is not set entirely by steroid levels.

questions.stem: A student observes that a neurotransmitter can trigger muscle contraction within milliseconds, whereas the breast development produced by estradiol during puberty takes months to complete. Which of the following best explains the slower time course of estradiol's effects?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estradiol must first be converted to estrone within the target tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estradiol acts by regulating gene transcription and the translation of new proteins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol opens ligand-gated ion channels that inactivate very slowly

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estradiol is secreted only during the luteal phase of each ovarian cycle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Estradiol requires human chorionic gonadotropin before entering target cells

explanation.summary: Unlike rapidly acting neurotransmitters, estrogen and progesterone produce slow, lasting changes because they regulate gene transcription and protein translation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike neurotransmitters, which act very rapidly, the changes from estrogen and progesterone develop over a long period and have lasting effects. After traveling in serum to their targets, they regulate gene transcription and protein translation, and building new proteins takes far longer than opening a synaptic channel.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conversion between estradiol and estrone by 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase is a metabolic interconversion, not the reason genomic effects are slow.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Steroid hormones do not act through ligand-gated ion channels; that mechanism belongs to fast neurotransmission.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Estradiol is produced across the cycle, including by follicles before ovulation; secretion timing is not why its effects are slow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG rescues the corpus luteum in pregnancy; steroids enter cells by diffusing across the plasma membrane without any hCG requirement.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old competitive weightlifter comes to the clinic because he and his partner have been unable to conceive for 14 months. For the past 2 years he has self-administered injectable anabolic-androgenic steroids obtained at his gym. Examination shows well-developed musculature, blood pressure of 144/92 mm Hg, and small, soft testes bilaterally. Semen analysis shows a markedly decreased sperm count. Which of the following best explains his impaired spermatogenesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Suppressed gonadotropin secretion with low intratesticular testosterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elevated inhibin B secretion with selective suppression of LH

choices.label: C
choices.text: Autoimmune disruption of the blood-testis barrier and germ cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased 5-alpha-reductase activity within the seminiferous tubules

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acquired loss of androgen-receptor function in Sertoli cells

explanation.summary: Exogenous androgens suppress the HPG axis, lowering intratesticular testosterone and Sertoli-cell stimulation despite high circulating androgen levels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Exogenous androgens provide negative feedback to the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary, decreasing GnRH, LH, and FSH secretion. Reduced LH lowers Leydig-cell output, so intratesticular testosterone falls, and reduced FSH withdraws Sertoli-cell stimulation. Spermatogenesis requires FSH plus a high local testosterone concentration, so sperm production declines and the testes atrophy even though circulating androgen levels are high.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Inhibin B is secreted by Sertoli cells and selectively inhibits FSH, not LH; with Sertoli-cell suppression, inhibin B would fall rather than rise.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nothing in the history suggests autoimmune testicular injury; the findings are explained by hormonal suppression from the injected steroids.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Conversion of testosterone to DHT by 5-alpha-reductase is a normal target-tissue event and does not impair spermatogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Androgen receptors are intact; the problem is loss of gonadotropin drive and local testosterone, not receptor failure.

questions.stem: During male fetal development, differentiation of the penis, scrotum, and prostate is primarily induced by which of the following hormones?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Testosterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dihydrotestosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dehydroepiandrosterone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Androstenedione

explanation.summary: DHT masculinizes the external genitalia and prostate, while testosterone masculinizes the Wolffian-duct derivatives.
explanation.whyCorrect: DHT, formed from testosterone by 5-alpha-reductase in target tissues, induces differentiation of the penis, scrotum, prostate, and male urethra during fetal development. It is a more potent androgen-receptor agonist than testosterone and acts largely within the tissues where it is produced.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Testosterone directly induces the Wolffian-duct derivatives (epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal vesicles), not the external genitalia and prostate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estradiol, formed by aromatization of testosterone, promotes epiphyseal plate maturation and closure rather than masculinizing external genitalia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: DHEA is a weak adrenal androgen contributing to pubic and axillary hair, body odor, and sebaceous activity, mainly after peripheral conversion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Androstenedione is a weak precursor androgen that must be converted to testosterone or estrogens to exert significant effects.

questions.stem: A study of male reproductive development examines the hormonal requirements for differentiation of the epididymis, ductus deferens, and seminal vesicles from the Wolffian ducts. Differentiation of these structures depends most directly on which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Testosterone secreted by fetal Leydig cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dihydrotestosterone formed in genital skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibin B secreted by fetal Sertoli cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: DHEAS secreted by the fetal adrenal gland

choices.label: E
choices.text: Estradiol formed by aromatization in peripheral tissues

explanation.summary: Testosterone from fetal Leydig cells drives Wolffian-duct differentiation into the epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal vesicles, and ejaculatory ducts.
explanation.whyCorrect: During fetal development, testicular testosterone production supports differentiation of the Wolffian-duct structures, including the epididymides, vasa deferentia, seminal vesicles, and ejaculatory ducts. This is a direct action of testosterone, distinct from the DHT-dependent masculinization of the external genitalia and prostate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DHT mediates differentiation of the penis, scrotum, prostate, and male urethra, not the Wolffian-duct derivatives.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin B regulates pituitary FSH secretion; it does not induce differentiation of Wolffian-duct structures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adrenal DHEAS is a weak androgen precursor whose main contributions are pubic and axillary hair, body odor, and sebaceous activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estradiol from aromatization of testosterone contributes to epiphyseal maturation and negative feedback, not Wolffian-duct differentiation.

questions.stem: In a physiology experiment, a healthy 25-year-old man receives a continuous infusion of inhibin B at a concentration sufficient to act on the pituitary. Which of the following changes in his hormone levels is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased FSH with LH and testosterone relatively unchanged

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased LH with FSH relatively unchanged

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreased FSH with a marked fall in testosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased FSH and increased LH

choices.label: E
choices.text: Decreased GnRH pulses with loss of both gonadotropins

explanation.summary: Inhibin B acts primarily on the anterior pituitary to selectively decrease FSH secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inhibin B, normally secreted by Sertoli cells, selectively inhibits FSH secretion at the anterior pituitary. Because the LH-Leydig-cell branch is regulated chiefly by sex-steroid feedback rather than by inhibin, LH and testosterone remain relatively unchanged while FSH falls.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Inhibin B does not selectively suppress LH; LH secretion is governed mainly by testosterone and estradiol feedback.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Testosterone production is driven by LH, which inhibin B does not suppress, so a marked fall in testosterone is not expected.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B is inhibitory to the pituitary; it does not raise gonadotropin secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibin B acts primarily at the anterior pituitary on FSH; it is not described as shutting down hypothalamic GnRH pulses or both gonadotropins.

questions.stem: During the first half of gestation, Leydig cells in a male fetus actively secrete testosterone, supporting differentiation of the internal genital ducts before the fetal hypothalamic-pituitary axis is fully mature. At this stage, Leydig-cell testosterone synthesis is stimulated primarily by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: LH from the fetal anterior pituitary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: C
choices.text: FSH from the fetal anterior pituitary

choices.label: D
choices.text: ACTH from the fetal anterior pituitary

choices.label: E
choices.text: GnRH acting directly on the testis

explanation.summary: Fetal Leydig cells synthesize testosterone in response to hCG; LH takes over this role after puberty.
explanation.whyCorrect: Leydig cells respond to hCG during fetal development and to LH after puberty. hCG activates LH receptors on Leydig cells, driving the testosterone production that supports fetal Wolffian-duct differentiation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: LH becomes the principal Leydig-cell stimulus after puberty; during fetal development the stimulus is hCG.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSH acts on Sertoli cells within the seminiferous tubules, not on Leydig-cell testosterone synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ACTH regulates adrenal-cortex steroid output, including adrenal androgens at adrenarche, not testicular testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GnRH acts on gonadotropes in the anterior pituitary via the portal circulation; it does not directly stimulate the testis.

questions.stem: A researcher measuring sex-steroid levels in healthy adult men notes that testosterone, like other steroid hormones, has a lipid-soluble four-ring structure that does not dissolve freely in plasma. In the bloodstream, most circulating testosterone is transported in which of the following ways?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bound to sex hormone-binding globulin or albumin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Freely dissolved in the aqueous plasma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bound to circulating inhibin B

choices.label: D
choices.text: Carried within circulating erythrocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Covalently attached to androgen receptors

explanation.summary: Most circulating testosterone travels bound to sex hormone-binding globulin or albumin; only a small unbound fraction is available to tissues.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because their fused steroid rings make them lipophilic, androgens cannot dissolve freely in plasma. Binding to sex hormone-binding globulin or albumin permits transport in the aqueous bloodstream and regulates the small unbound fraction that can diffuse into target cells.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Only a small fraction of testosterone circulates unbound; its lipophilicity prevents most of it from dissolving freely in plasma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin B is a Sertoli-cell hormone that regulates FSH; it is not a plasma carrier for testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testosterone is carried by plasma binding proteins, not inside red blood cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Androgen receptors are intracellular; testosterone binds them noncovalently after entering the target cell, not during transport.

questions.stem: In a prostate epithelial cell, testosterone diffuses across the plasma membrane and is converted by 5-alpha-reductase to DHT, which binds an intracellular androgen receptor. Which of the following events occurs next in this signaling pathway?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The receptor complex dimerizes, enters the nucleus, and binds androgen-response elements

choices.label: B
choices.text: The receptor activates a membrane-bound G protein that raises cyclic AMP

choices.label: C
choices.text: The receptor opens a ligand-gated cation channel in the plasma membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: The receptor phosphorylates tyrosine residues on cytosolic substrate proteins

choices.label: E
choices.text: The receptor complex blocks translation of target mRNAs at the ribosome

explanation.summary: Activated androgen receptors translocate to the nucleus, dimerize, bind androgen-response elements, and regulate gene transcription.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testosterone or DHT binds an intracellular androgen receptor; the activated receptor translocates to the nucleus, forms dimers, binds androgen-response elements in DNA, and regulates transcription of target genes into mRNA that is then translated into protein. In the prostate, DHT is the predominant androgen-receptor ligand.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Androgen receptors are nuclear transcription regulators, not G protein-coupled receptors that signal through cyclic AMP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Androgens act through intracellular receptors that alter transcription, not through ligand-gated ion channels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The androgen receptor is not a tyrosine kinase; its action is to regulate gene transcription.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The activated receptor regulates transcription of target genes; it does not act by blocking translation at the ribosome.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old patient with a 46,XY karyotype is evaluated for absent pubertal virilization. Examination shows female-pattern external genitalia, and imaging reveals intra-abdominal testes. Circulating testosterone is within the adult male reference range, and a trial of androgen therapy produces no virilization. Which of the following best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nonfunctional intracellular androgen receptors in target tissues

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deficient 5-alpha-reductase activity in genital skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Absent Leydig-cell testosterone synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failure of hCG stimulation during fetal life

choices.label: E
choices.text: Excess aromatization of testosterone to estradiol

explanation.summary: In complete androgen insensitivity syndrome, a 46,XY individual with testes has nonfunctional androgen receptors, so androgen-dependent masculinization cannot occur.
explanation.whyCorrect: Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome results from nonfunctional androgen receptors in a 46,XY individual with testes. Androgens are produced but cannot act, so external genital development follows a typically female pattern. Because the receptor itself is defective, giving more androgen is ineffective, which explains the failed therapeutic trial.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A 5-alpha-reductase problem would leave receptor-mediated testosterone actions intact, so a trial of androgen therapy would not be entirely without effect; the complete unresponsiveness points to the receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Circulating testosterone is in the adult male range, so Leydig-cell synthesis is clearly preserved.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testes formed and produce testosterone, so fetal Leydig-cell stimulation was adequate; the defect is downstream at the receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The findings reflect absent androgen action rather than excess estrogen production; the key clue is that androgen treatment is ineffective.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with a 20-year history of heavy daily alcohol use reports decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Examination shows bilateral, tender enlargement of glandular breast tissue. Along with suppression of GnRH and LH secretion, which of the following mechanisms best explains his breast findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Impaired hepatic metabolism and clearance of estrogens

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased pulsatile GnRH secretion from the hypothalamus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess inhibin B secretion from Sertoli cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased Leydig-cell testosterone production

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enhanced 5-alpha-reduction of testosterone in breast tissue

explanation.summary: Chronic alcohol use suppresses the HPG axis and, through liver dysfunction, impairs estrogen clearance, producing increased estrogenic effects such as gynecomastia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic alcohol use lowers testosterone by decreasing hypothalamic GnRH release, directly inhibiting pituitary LH secretion, and impairing Leydig- and Sertoli-cell function. Alcohol-associated liver dysfunction additionally impairs hepatic estrogen metabolism and clearance, so estrogenic effects increase, which can produce loss of libido, sexual dysfunction, and gynecomastia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Alcohol decreases GnRH release from the hypothalamus; it does not increase it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chronic alcohol use impairs Sertoli-cell function; rising inhibin B is not the mechanism, and inhibin B acts on FSH rather than causing breast growth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Alcohol reduces Leydig-cell stimulation and testosterone production; increased testosterone output would not explain this picture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DHT formation drives androgenic effects such as prostate growth and balding; gynecomastia here reflects excess estrogenic effect from poor hepatic clearance.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old girl is brought to the clinic because of new body odor and a small amount of pubic hair. She has no breast development, and her growth curve is unchanged. Increased secretion of which of the following best accounts for these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DHEA and DHEAS from the adrenal cortex

choices.label: B
choices.text: Testosterone from ovarian theca cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol from the ovaries

choices.label: D
choices.text: LH and FSH from the anterior pituitary

choices.label: E
choices.text: DHT produced within genital skin

explanation.summary: Adrenarche, driven by ACTH-regulated adrenal androgen output, precedes gonadal puberty and produces pubic and axillary hair, body odor, and sebaceous activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: During adrenarche, the adrenal cortex becomes the principal source of rising circulating androgens under ACTH regulation, before gonadal puberty begins. Adrenal androgens such as DHEA and DHEAS contribute to pubic and axillary hair growth, body odor, and sebaceous-gland activity, partly through peripheral conversion to more potent androgens.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ovarian theca-cell androgen production is stimulated by LH with gonadal puberty; the absence of breast development indicates the gonadal axis has not yet activated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rising estradiol would produce breast development, which is absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gonadotropin activation marks gonadal puberty; adrenarche occurs before it and is ACTH-regulated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Local DHT formation is downstream of available androgen precursors; the primary change at adrenarche is increased adrenal DHEA and DHEAS output.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy completing puberty is noted to have progressive slowing of linear growth as his skeletal maturation advances. The maturation and closure of his epiphyseal growth plates is promoted primarily by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estradiol formed by aromatization of testosterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: DHT formed by 5-alpha-reduction of testosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Testosterone acting directly on androgen receptors in bone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibin B secreted by Sertoli cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: DHEAS secreted by the adrenal cortex

explanation.summary: Aromatization of testosterone to estradiol promotes epiphyseal plate maturation and closure at the end of puberty.
explanation.whyCorrect: While testosterone contributes to voice deepening, libido, muscle growth, and spermatogenesis, its conversion by aromatase to estradiol is what promotes epiphyseal plate maturation and closure, ending linear growth as puberty completes.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DHT mediates prostate growth, male-pattern balding, and sebaceous activity, not epiphyseal closure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epiphyseal maturation is attributed to estradiol produced from testosterone, not to direct androgen-receptor action of testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B regulates pituitary FSH secretion and has no described role in growth-plate closure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adrenal DHEAS is a weak androgen precursor contributing to hair, odor, and sebaceous activity, not epiphyseal closure.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old male cyclist is found on routine laboratory testing to have a hemoglobin of 18.6 g/dL and a hematocrit of 56%. He is well hydrated, has no lung disease, and lives at sea level. He reports 8 months of daily use of an unprescribed powder containing "male hormones" that his trainer supplied. Which of the following best explains his laboratory findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Androgen-stimulated increase in red-blood-cell production

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic arterial hypoxemia stimulating erythropoiesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythropoietin secretion from a renal tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hemoconcentration from reduced plasma volume

choices.label: E
choices.text: A primary clonal myeloproliferative disorder

explanation.summary: Supraphysiologic androgen exposure increases red-blood-cell production and can cause erythrocytosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Androgens support erythropoiesis during adulthood, and although erythropoietin is the principal hormonal regulator of red-cell production, supraphysiologic androgen exposure can increase red-blood-cell production and cause erythrocytosis. In a patient taking an unprescribed androgen-containing supplement, the elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit are best explained by this androgen effect.

whyWrongByChoice.B: He has no lung disease and lives at sea level, so chronic hypoxemia is not a plausible driver of his erythrocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: There is no evidence of a renal mass; the temporal link to androgen use points to the supplement as the cause.
whyWrongByChoice.D: He is well hydrated, so a spurious rise in hematocrit from reduced plasma volume is unlikely.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A clonal marrow disorder is not suggested when a known erythrocytosis-producing exposure, supraphysiologic androgens, accounts for the findings.

questions.stem: In an investigation of Leydig-cell steroidogenesis, researchers identify the step that delivers cholesterol into mitochondria so that testosterone synthesis can proceed. This step is mediated by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Steroidogenic acute regulatory (StAR) protein

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme (P450scc)

choices.label: C
choices.text: 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sex hormone-binding globulin

choices.label: E
choices.text: 5-alpha-reductase

explanation.summary: Testosterone synthesis in Leydig cells requires StAR protein-mediated transport of cholesterol into mitochondria.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Leydig-cell pathway that converts cholesterol to testosterone requires steroidogenic acute regulatory (StAR) protein-mediated transport of cholesterol into mitochondria. Only after this delivery step can the steroidogenic enzymes, beginning with cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme, act on cholesterol to generate testosterone.

whyWrongByChoice.B: P450scc is a steroidogenic enzyme that acts on cholesterol; it does not transport cholesterol into mitochondria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase is one of the downstream steroidogenic enzymes in the pathway, not a cholesterol transporter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sex hormone-binding globulin carries testosterone in plasma; it has no role in intracellular cholesterol movement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 5-alpha-reductase converts testosterone to DHT in target tissues; it does not participate in mitochondrial cholesterol transport.

questions.stem: A biochemist studying steroidogenesis notes that testosterone shares a fused four-ring nucleus with the other steroid hormones. Synthesis of androgens and the other steroid hormones begins with which of the following precursor molecules?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cholesterol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dehydroepiandrosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Androstenedione

choices.label: D
choices.text: Androstenediol

choices.label: E
choices.text: Estradiol

explanation.summary: Cholesterol is the sterol precursor for androgen and all other steroid-hormone synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cholesterol is a sterol that serves as the precursor for androgen and other steroid-hormone synthesis, and cholesterol and the steroid hormones share the same four-ring steroid nucleus. In Leydig cells, cholesterol is converted through a series of steroidogenic reactions to testosterone.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DHEA is a weak adrenal androgen and an intermediate precursor; it is itself synthesized downstream of cholesterol.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Androstenedione is a weak androgen intermediate convertible to testosterone or estrogens, not the starting precursor of steroidogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Androstenediol is a weak androgenic steroid and metabolic intermediate, not the initial substrate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estradiol is a product formed from testosterone by aromatization, not the precursor for steroid-hormone synthesis.

questions.stem: A physiologist plots testicular androgen production in males from fetal life through adolescence. Which of the following patterns best describes the expected course?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activity in fetal life, a transient increase in early infancy, relative quiescence in childhood, and a rise at puberty

choices.label: B
choices.text: Quiescence in fetal life, a steady climb through infancy and childhood, and a plateau reached at puberty

choices.label: C
choices.text: Activity in fetal life, sustained high output through infancy and childhood, and a further rise at puberty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Quiescence in fetal life, a surge in infancy, sustained output through childhood, and a decline at puberty

choices.label: E
choices.text: Activity in fetal life, quiescence from birth through childhood, and a first postnatal increase appearing only at puberty

explanation.summary: Testicular androgen production is active in fetal life, transiently increases in early infancy, becomes relatively quiescent during childhood, and increases again at puberty.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testicular androgen production is active during fetal development, transiently increases during early infancy, becomes relatively quiescent during childhood, and increases again at puberty. After puberty, testicular testosterone production generally continues through adulthood but may decline with age and changes in health.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Testicular androgen production is active during fetal development, when hCG stimulates Leydig cells; it does not begin from quiescence at birth.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Childhood is a period of relative quiescence, not sustained high output.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fetal life is a period of active production, and puberty brings a rise rather than a decline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This pattern omits the transient increase in testicular androgen production that occurs during early infancy.

questions.stem: During an evaluation of ovarian steroid production in a healthy premenopausal woman, androgen synthesis in the theca cells of the ovary is found to be stimulated primarily by which of the following hormones?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Follicle-stimulating hormone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adrenocorticotropic hormone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibin B

explanation.summary: LH stimulates androgen synthesis in ovarian theca cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: In females, the ovaries produce testosterone directly and also produce androstenedione, which can be converted into testosterone. Luteinizing hormone stimulates androgen synthesis in ovarian theca cells, paralleling its stimulation of testosterone synthesis in testicular Leydig cells.

whyWrongByChoice.B: FSH acts on Sertoli cells in the male; it is not the described stimulus for theca-cell androgen synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: ACTH regulates adrenal androgen output, which rises at adrenarche; it does not drive ovarian theca-cell synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GnRH acts on gonadotropes in the anterior pituitary via the portal circulation, not directly on the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibin B is an inhibitory feedback signal that decreases pituitary FSH secretion; it does not stimulate theca-cell androgen synthesis.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman whose ovarian steroid production has substantially declined still has measurable circulating testosterone. Compared with earlier in her reproductive life, her circulating testosterone now derives proportionally more from which of the following sources?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conversion of DHEA and androstenedione in fat, skin, and liver

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct secretion of testosterone by ovarian theca cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aromatization of circulating estradiol into testosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Secretion of testosterone by anterior-pituitary gonadotropes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Release of testosterone stored bound to plasma SHBG

explanation.summary: Peripheral conversion of androgen precursors becomes proportionally more important as ovarian steroid production declines.
explanation.whyCorrect: In tissues such as fat, skin, and liver, precursor hormones, especially DHEA and androstenedione, are converted into testosterone. This peripheral conversion contributes to circulating testosterone across reproductive life and becomes proportionally more important as ovarian steroid production declines.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ovarian secretion is the source that has declined; it contributes proportionally less, not more.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aromatization runs in the opposite direction, converting testosterone to estradiol; estradiol is not converted back to testosterone by aromatase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gonadotropes secrete the peptide gonadotropins LH and FSH, not steroid hormones such as testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SHBG binding is a transport arrangement in plasma, not a storage source that generates new testosterone.

questions.stem: A newborn assigned female at birth is noted to have virilized external genitalia. Evaluation leads to a diagnosis of congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Which of the following best explains the virilization?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated adrenal androgen production

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess ovarian testosterone secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nonfunctional androgen receptors in target tissues

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased peripheral aromatization of androgens to estrogens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Deficient hepatic clearance of estrogens

explanation.summary: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia elevates adrenal androgen levels, which can virilize individuals assigned female at birth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia can lead to elevated androgen levels arising from the adrenal gland, which makes androgens in both males and females. The excess androgens may result in development of traits typically associated with male sex characteristics in individuals assigned female at birth.

whyWrongByChoice.B: CAH is an adrenal disorder; the ovary is not the source of the androgen excess in this condition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nonfunctional androgen receptors describe complete androgen insensitivity syndrome, which prevents virilization rather than causing it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Conversion of androgens to estrogens would reduce, not produce, androgen-dependent virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Impaired estrogen clearance increases estrogenic effects such as gynecomastia; it does not virilize a newborn.

questions.stem: In a postpubertal male, gonadotropin-releasing hormone released in pulses from the hypothalamus stimulates secretion of LH and FSH. GnRH reaches its target gonadotrope cells by which of the following routes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Through the hypothalamic-pituitary portal circulation to the anterior pituitary

choices.label: B
choices.text: By axonal transport to the posterior pituitary for storage and release

choices.label: C
choices.text: Through the systemic circulation directly to receptors on Leydig cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: By diffusion through the cerebrospinal fluid to the pituitary gland

choices.label: E
choices.text: By retrograde flow from the posterior lobe into the anterior lobe

explanation.summary: Pulsatile GnRH travels through the hypothalamic-pituitary portal circulation to stimulate gonadotropes in the anterior pituitary.
explanation.whyCorrect: The hypothalamus releases GnRH in pulses. GnRH then travels through the hypothalamic-pituitary portal circulation and stimulates gonadotropes in the anterior pituitary to secrete the two gonadotropins, luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone.

whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH acts on the anterior pituitary via the portal system; it is not carried by axons to the posterior pituitary for release.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GnRH does not act directly on the testis; LH, secreted by the pituitary in response to GnRH, is the hormone that stimulates Leydig cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GnRH delivery to gonadotropes occurs through the portal blood vessels, not by diffusion through cerebrospinal fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The described route is the hypothalamic-pituitary portal circulation, not retrograde flow between pituitary lobes.

questions.stem: In an experimental study, the circulating testosterone concentration of a healthy 30-year-old man is abruptly lowered while the rest of his endocrine system is initially undisturbed. Over the following period, which of the following changes in hormone secretion is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased GnRH and LH secretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased GnRH and LH secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased inhibin B secretion from Sertoli cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Selective suppression of FSH secretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of GnRH pulsatility with unchanged gonadotropins

explanation.summary: When testosterone falls, its negative feedback diminishes, allowing GnRH and LH secretion to rise and stabilize testosterone production.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the testosterone feedback loop, testosterone and its aromatization to estradiol provide negative feedback to the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary, reducing GnRH and LH secretion. When testosterone decreases, this inhibition diminishes, allowing GnRH and LH secretion to rise; this loop stabilizes testosterone production.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Decreased GnRH and LH is the response to a rise in sex-steroid feedback, not to a fall in testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin B reflects FSH-driven Sertoli-cell activity and spermatogenesis; a fall in circulating testosterone does not stimulate its secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FSH suppression is produced by inhibin B feedback; low testosterone relieves rather than adds pituitary inhibition.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Low testosterone releases the axis from inhibition; it does not abolish GnRH pulses while leaving gonadotropins unchanged.

questions.stem: A patient sustains selective damage to the Sertoli cells of both testes, while Leydig-cell function remains intact. Which of the following hormonal patterns is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased FSH with relatively preserved testosterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased FSH with decreased testosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreased FSH with increased testosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased LH with decreased FSH

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased inhibin B with decreased LH

explanation.summary: Loss of Sertoli-cell inhibin B removes selective FSH inhibition, so FSH rises while intact Leydig cells keep testosterone relatively preserved.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sertoli cells secrete inhibin B, which acts primarily on the anterior pituitary to selectively decrease FSH secretion. With Sertoli-cell damage, inhibin B falls and FSH secretion increases. Because the LH-Leydig-cell branch is regulated by sex-steroid feedback and Leydig cells are intact, testosterone remains relatively preserved.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Loss of inhibin B raises FSH rather than lowering it, and intact Leydig cells maintain testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSH increases when inhibin B feedback is lost, and there is no stimulus here for testosterone to rise above normal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: With preserved testosterone feedback, LH is not expected to increase, and FSH rises rather than falls.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Damaged Sertoli cells produce less inhibin B, not more, and inhibin B regulates FSH rather than LH.

questions.stem: Developing germ cells in the adluminal compartment of the seminiferous tubule express antigens that could provoke an immune response. These cells are shielded from immune exposure primarily by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tight junctions between adjacent Sertoli cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tight junctions between adjacent Leydig cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Binding of germ-cell surface antigens to SHBG

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibin B-mediated suppression of FSH secretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: The high local concentration of testosterone

explanation.summary: Sertoli-cell tight junctions form the blood-testis barrier, separating basal and adluminal compartments and limiting immune exposure to developing germ cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sertoli cells form tight junctions that create the blood-testis barrier. This barrier separates the basal and adluminal compartments of the seminiferous tubule and limits immune exposure to developing germ cells.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Leydig cells lie outside the seminiferous tubules and synthesize testosterone; the barrier is formed by Sertoli-cell tight junctions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: SHBG is a plasma transport protein for androgens; it does not sequester germ-cell antigens.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B regulates pituitary FSH secretion; it does not create a physical barrier around germ cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: High intratesticular testosterone supports Sertoli-cell functions for spermatogenesis, but immune protection comes from the tight-junction barrier.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism wishes to father a child. His physician selects gonadotropin therapy that includes hCG rather than exogenous testosterone. Compared with exogenous testosterone, hCG offers which of the following advantages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It maintains intratesticular testosterone by activating Leydig-cell LH receptors

choices.label: B
choices.text: It selectively increases FSH secretion from the anterior pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: It binds androgen receptors directly without requiring the testis

choices.label: D
choices.text: It restores pulsatile GnRH release from the hypothalamus

choices.label: E
choices.text: It prevents aromatization of testosterone to estradiol in tissues

explanation.summary: hCG activates LH receptors on Leydig cells and can maintain intratesticular testosterone, unlike exogenous testosterone, which suppresses it.
explanation.whyCorrect: hCG activates LH receptors on Leydig cells and stimulates testicular testosterone production. Unlike exogenous testosterone, which suppresses GnRH, LH, and FSH and thereby lowers intratesticular testosterone and spermatogenesis, hCG can maintain intratesticular testosterone and may be used as part of gonadotropin therapy in selected patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism or infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.B: hCG acts on LH receptors in the testis; it does not stimulate pituitary FSH secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG is a gonadotropin that drives Leydig-cell steroidogenesis; it is not an androgen-receptor ligand.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hCG acts at the testis, downstream of the hypothalamus; it does not restore GnRH pulsatility.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG does not block aromatase; aromatization of testosterone to estradiol is a normal downstream event.

questions.stem: A pharmacology student compares the two principal active androgens. Compared with testosterone, dihydrotestosterone is best characterized as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A more potent receptor agonist formed and acting within target tissues

choices.label: B
choices.text: A weaker receptor agonist distributed mainly in the circulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: The major circulating androgen bound to plasma proteins

choices.label: D
choices.text: A precursor requiring conversion to testosterone for activity

choices.label: E
choices.text: An estrogen-receptor ligand generated by aromatase activity

explanation.summary: DHT is a more potent androgen-receptor agonist than testosterone and is produced locally by 5-alpha-reduction, acting largely within the tissue where it is made.
explanation.whyCorrect: DHT is a more potent androgen-receptor agonist than testosterone and is produced primarily within target tissues by 5-alpha-reduction of testosterone. Because DHT is formed and metabolized locally, much of its action occurs within the tissue in which it is produced, whereas testosterone is the major circulating androgen.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DHT is more potent than testosterone at the androgen receptor, and its distribution is local rather than mainly circulatory.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Testosterone, not DHT, is the major circulating androgen carried by plasma binding proteins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: DHT is a product of testosterone conversion, not a precursor of it, and it is directly active at the androgen receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DHT is generated by 5-alpha-reductase and acts on androgen receptors; aromatase generates estradiol from testosterone.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old man has gradual enlargement of the prostate gland along with thinning of scalp hair in a male pattern. Both of these later-life processes are promoted chiefly by which of the following androgens?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dihydrotestosterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Testosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dehydroepiandrosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Androstenedione

choices.label: E
choices.text: Androstenediol

explanation.summary: Later in life, DHT contributes to prostate growth, male-pattern balding, and increased sebaceous-gland activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: DHT, formed from testosterone by 5-alpha-reductase within target tissues, contributes later in life to prostate growth, male-pattern balding, and increased sebaceous-gland activity. In the prostate, DHT is the predominant androgen-receptor ligand.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Testosterone supports spermatogenesis, skeletal-muscle growth, libido, and erythropoiesis; the prostate and balding effects are attributed to its 5-alpha-reduced product, DHT.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DHEA is a weak adrenal androgen contributing to pubic and axillary hair, body odor, and sebaceous activity, mainly through peripheral conversion.
