whyWrongByChoice.D: Androstenedione is a weak precursor androgen that must be converted to testosterone or estrogens for significant effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Androstenediol is a weak androgenic steroid and metabolic intermediate, not the driver of prostate growth and balding.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old female athlete has been self-administering anabolic-androgenic steroids for the past year to improve her competitive performance. Which of the following sets of adverse effects is most likely to develop?

choices.label: A
choices.text: New facial hair growth and a deepened voice

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breast enlargement and nipple discharge

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased scalp hair density and softer skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: A higher-pitched voice and loss of body hair

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced sebaceous activity and clearing of acne

explanation.summary: In females, anabolic-androgenic steroid use can cause excess body and facial hair, male-pattern baldness, menstrual changes, and a deepened voice.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adverse effects of anabolic-androgenic steroids in females include excess body and facial hair, male-pattern baldness, menstrual changes, and a deepened voice. These reflect systemic androgenic effects of the exogenous steroids.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gynecomastia is an adverse effect described in males using these agents; androgen excess in a female does not produce breast enlargement and discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Androgen excess promotes male-pattern scalp hair loss and increased sebaceous activity, not denser scalp hair and softer skin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Androgens deepen the voice and increase body hair; they do not raise voice pitch or remove body hair.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Severe acne and increased sebaceous activity are recognized adverse effects; androgens do not clear acne.

questions.stem: Testosterone and other anabolic-androgenic agents are sometimes used with a prescription and sometimes without one. Which of the following individuals has an accepted medical indication for prescribed androgen therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An adolescent male with delayed puberty due to hypogonadism

choices.label: B
choices.text: A healthy adult bodybuilder seeking increased muscle mass

choices.label: C
choices.text: A competitive cyclist seeking faster recovery from training

choices.label: D
choices.text: A healthy man pursuing a cosmetic increase in lean physique

choices.label: E
choices.text: A healthy woman seeking improved athletic performance

explanation.summary: Testosterone may be prescribed to induce pubertal development in males with delayed puberty or hypogonadism; performance and cosmetic use is unprescribed use with real risks.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testosterone may be prescribed to induce pubertal development in males with delayed puberty or hypogonadism and to treat selected symptoms of androgen deficiency. Selected anabolic-androgenic agents have also been used to treat severe loss of lean body mass, as in patients with AIDS or cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Muscle building in a healthy person is a common form of unprescribed use, carrying reproductive and systemic risks rather than constituting a medical indication.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Use for recovery from training or injury in a healthy competitor is a competitive, unprescribed use, not an accepted indication.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cosmetic enhancement of physique in a healthy person is not a medical indication for androgen therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Performance enhancement in a healthy athlete is unprescribed use and exposes females to virilizing adverse effects.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man who has taken an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid preparation for 9 months is found to have mildly elevated liver enzymes. He does not drink alcohol and takes no other medications or supplements. Which of the following best explains his laboratory abnormality?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hepatotoxicity associated with the steroid preparation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alcohol-associated liver dysfunction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hepatic congestion caused by erythrocytosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Impaired hepatic clearance of circulating estrogens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased hepatic aromatization of testosterone

explanation.summary: Some anabolic-androgenic steroid preparations cause hepatotoxicity, one of the recognized systemic adverse effects of their use.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adverse effects of anabolic-androgenic steroids include hepatotoxicity with some preparations, along with severe acne, mood changes, erythrocytosis, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and increased cardiovascular risk. In a steroid user without other exposures, the elevated liver enzymes are best attributed to the preparation itself.

whyWrongByChoice.B: He does not drink alcohol, so alcohol-associated liver dysfunction cannot account for the findings.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythrocytosis is a separate adverse effect of androgen exposure; it is not described as a cause of hepatic injury.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Impaired estrogen clearance is a consequence of liver dysfunction that raises estrogenic effects; it is not the cause of elevated liver enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aromatization of testosterone is a normal metabolic conversion, not a hepatotoxic process.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy in mid-puberty develops progressive deepening of his voice as his larynx changes. This pubertal effect is attributed primarily to which of the following hormones?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Testosterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dihydrotestosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dehydroepiandrosterone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibin B

explanation.summary: Testosterone drives pubertal voice deepening via the larynx, along with skeletal-muscle development and libido.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the pubertal changes produced by activation of the HPG axis, voice deepening via the larynx and skeletal-muscle development are musculoskeletal effects of testosterone. Testosterone contributes to voice deepening and libido, while other androgen effects are delegated to DHT or to estradiol formed by aromatization.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DHT mediates growth of the prostate, male-pattern balding, and sebaceous-gland activity, not laryngeal voice deepening.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estradiol formed from testosterone promotes epiphyseal plate maturation and closure rather than voice change.
whyWrongByChoice.D: DHEA is a weak adrenal androgen contributing to pubic and axillary hair, body odor, and sebaceous activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibin B is a Sertoli-cell hormone that regulates FSH secretion; it has no laryngeal action.

questions.stem: An endocrinology fellow is reviewing the less potent androgens and their metabolic fates. Which of the following best characterizes androstenedione?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A weak androgen convertible to testosterone or estrogens

choices.label: B
choices.text: The most potent endogenous androgen-receptor agonist

choices.label: C
choices.text: The principal plasma carrier protein for testosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: A Sertoli-cell peptide that selectively suppresses FSH

choices.label: E
choices.text: The predominant androgen-receptor ligand in the prostate

explanation.summary: Androstenedione is a weak androgen and a precursor that can be converted to testosterone or estrogens.
explanation.whyCorrect: Androstenedione is a weak androgen and a precursor that can be converted to testosterone or estrogens. The ovaries produce it as one route to testosterone, and peripheral tissues such as fat, skin, and liver convert it into testosterone.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DHT, not androstenedione, is the most potent androgen-receptor agonist described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sex hormone-binding globulin and albumin are the plasma carriers of testosterone; androstenedione is a steroid, not a carrier protein.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B is the Sertoli-cell hormone that selectively suppresses FSH; androstenedione is not a peptide.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DHT is the predominant androgen-receptor ligand in the prostate.

questions.stem: A laboratory measures total testosterone in a healthy 35-year-old man. Most of the testosterone circulating in his blood originated from which of the following sources?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leydig cells of the testes

choices.label: B
choices.text: The adrenal cortex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sertoli cells of the testes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peripheral conversion of DHEA in fat and skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gonadotropes of the anterior pituitary

explanation.summary: The testes, via Leydig cells, produce most circulating testosterone in adult males.
explanation.whyCorrect: The testes produce most circulating testosterone in adult males, and within the testes it is the Leydig cells that synthesize testosterone from cholesterol in response to LH. Adrenal and peripheral sources are proportionally more important in females.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The adrenal cortex contributes weaker androgens such as DHEA and DHEAS; it is not the main source of circulating testosterone in adult males.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sertoli cells support spermatogenesis and secrete inhibin B; Leydig cells are the testosterone-producing cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral conversion of precursors contributes to circulating testosterone but is not the predominant source in an adult male.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gonadotropes secrete LH and FSH, peptide hormones that regulate the testis; they do not produce testosterone.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old premenopausal woman has her circulating testosterone measured during an endocrine evaluation. Her circulating testosterone is best described as coming from which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ovarian and adrenal secretion plus peripheral conversion of precursors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ovarian secretion alone, with no adrenal or peripheral contribution

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adrenal secretion alone, with no ovarian or peripheral contribution

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peripheral conversion alone, with no direct glandular secretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Anterior-pituitary secretion supplemented by hepatic synthesis

explanation.summary: In premenopausal females, circulating testosterone comes from direct ovarian and adrenal secretion and from peripheral conversion of androgen precursors.
explanation.whyCorrect: In premenopausal females, circulating testosterone comes from direct ovarian and adrenal secretion and from peripheral conversion of androgen precursors. The ovaries secrete testosterone directly and also produce androstenedione that can be converted to testosterone, while tissues such as fat, skin, and liver convert DHEA and androstenedione into testosterone.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The ovary is only one contributor; the adrenal glands and peripheral conversion also supply circulating testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The adrenal gland is not the sole source; ovarian secretion and peripheral conversion contribute as well.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral conversion supplements, but does not replace, direct ovarian and adrenal secretion in premenopausal women.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The anterior pituitary secretes peptide gonadotropins, not testosterone, and the liver's role is conversion of precursors rather than a paired glandular source.

questions.stem: A healthy 78-year-old man asks whether his hormone levels should be the same as when he was younger. Compared with his testosterone concentration at age 30, his current total testosterone is most likely which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lower, reflecting a general decline with aging

choices.label: B
choices.text: Higher, reflecting cumulative lifetime secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Identical, because adult levels are fixed after puberty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Undetectable, because Leydig cells are lost in midlife

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cyclic, varying with a monthly gonadal rhythm

explanation.summary: Testosterone rises at puberty, remains within the adult range during much of reproductive adulthood, and generally declines with aging.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testosterone concentrations rise at puberty, remain within the adult range during much of reproductive adulthood, and generally decline with aging. Testicular testosterone production continues through adulthood but may decline with age and changes in health.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Testosterone is not cumulative; production generally declines rather than rises in late life.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adult levels are not fixed; a general age-related decline is expected.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Production declines gradually with aging; it does not cease abruptly, and testosterone remains measurable.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A monthly gonadal cycle is not a described feature of male testosterone regulation; the relevant change across late adulthood is gradual decline.

questions.stem: Within prostate epithelial cells, testosterone is converted to the more potent androgen dihydrotestosterone. This conversion is catalyzed by which of the following enzymes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 5-alpha-reductase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aromatase

choices.label: C
choices.text: 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme (P450scc)

choices.label: E
choices.text: 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase

explanation.summary: 5-alpha-reductase converts testosterone to DHT within target tissues that express the enzyme.
explanation.whyCorrect: In tissues that express 5-alpha-reductase, such as the prostate, testosterone is converted locally to DHT. Because DHT is formed and metabolized locally, much of its action occurs within the tissue in which it is produced, and in the prostate DHT is the predominant androgen-receptor ligand.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aromatase converts testosterone to estradiol, not to DHT.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase is a steroidogenic enzyme in the testosterone synthesis pathway within Leydig cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: P450scc acts on cholesterol early in steroidogenesis, well upstream of testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase is a steroidogenic enzyme in the cholesterol-to-testosterone pathway, not the testosterone-to-DHT step.

questions.stem: A hematology lecture contrasts the hormonal control of red-blood-cell production with the supportive role androgens play in adulthood. The principal hormonal regulator of erythropoiesis is which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Erythropoietin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Testosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dihydrotestosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibin B

explanation.summary: Erythropoietin is the principal hormonal regulator of erythropoiesis; androgens play a supportive role and cause erythrocytosis only at supraphysiologic exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Erythropoietin is the principal hormonal regulator of erythropoiesis. Androgens support erythropoiesis during adulthood, and supraphysiologic androgen exposure can increase red-blood-cell production and cause erythrocytosis, but this is a supportive and pharmacologic effect rather than the primary physiologic control.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Testosterone supports erythropoiesis but is not its principal hormonal regulator.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DHT's described actions involve the external genitalia, prostate, hair, and sebaceous glands, not primary control of red-cell production.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LH regulates Leydig-cell testosterone synthesis; it has no direct role in erythropoiesis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibin B selectively regulates pituitary FSH secretion and is unrelated to red-cell production.

questions.stem: In an experimental protocol, aromatization of testosterone to estradiol is selectively prevented in a healthy adult man while his circulating testosterone concentration is held constant. Which of the following changes in anterior-pituitary secretion is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased LH secretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased LH secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Unchanged LH with abolished FSH secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decreased FSH secretion driven by rising inhibin B

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of both gonadotropins from gonadotrope failure

explanation.summary: Estradiol formed by aromatization of testosterone contributes to negative feedback on GnRH and LH; removing it disinhibits LH secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the testosterone feedback loop, testosterone and its aromatization to estradiol provide negative feedback to the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary, reducing GnRH and LH secretion. Preventing aromatization removes the estradiol component of this feedback, so inhibition diminishes and LH secretion rises even though testosterone itself is unchanged.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Removing part of the negative feedback disinhibits the axis; LH secretion increases rather than decreases.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSH is chiefly regulated by inhibin B from Sertoli cells, which this intervention does not abolish.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nothing in this intervention stimulates Sertoli-cell inhibin B secretion; the primary effect is on the sex-steroid feedback loop.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gonadotropes remain functional; loss of one feedback signal increases rather than eliminates gonadotropin output.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman with regular 28-day cycles is on day 8 of her cycle. Serum estradiol is rising as a cohort of antral follicles grows. FSH most directly increases estradiol production during this phase by stimulating which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Androstenedione synthesis by theca cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aromatase activity in granulosa cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: GnRH pulse frequency in the hypothalamus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progesterone secretion by the corpus luteum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vascularization of the outer theca layer

explanation.summary: FSH stimulates granulosa-cell aromatase to convert theca-derived androstenedione to estradiol.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the two-cell mechanism, LH stimulates theca cells to produce androstenedione, which diffuses to granulosa cells. FSH then stimulates granulosa-cell aromatase to convert that androstenedione to estradiol, driving the follicular-phase estradiol rise.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Androstenedione production by theca cells is stimulated by LH, not FSH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GnRH originates in the hypothalamus and drives pituitary FSH release, not the reverse.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The corpus luteum does not exist during the follicular phase; it forms only after ovulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Theca vascularization is a structural feature of secondary-follicle development, not the direct FSH-dependent step in estradiol synthesis.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is on day 13 of a 28-day cycle. Serum studies show estradiol that has remained markedly elevated for the past two days, produced by a single dominant follicle. Which of the following hormonal events is most likely to occur next?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A surge in LH secretion from the anterior pituitary

choices.label: B
choices.text: A rise in FSH driven by increased inhibin B

choices.label: C
choices.text: A rise in trophoblast-derived hCG secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: A sustained fall in GnRH pulse activity

choices.label: E
choices.text: A sharp increase in progesterone from theca cells

explanation.summary: Sustained high estradiol late in the follicular phase switches to positive feedback and generates the preovulatory LH surge.
explanation.whyCorrect: During most of the follicular phase estradiol suppresses gonadotropin secretion, but sustained high estradiol late in the follicular phase produces positive feedback on the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary. This generates the LH surge that triggers ovulation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Inhibin B decreases FSH secretion rather than raising it; FSH is falling at this point in the cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG is produced by trophoblast cells only after implantation, not at midcycle in a nonpregnant woman.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sustained high estradiol produces positive feedback at the hypothalamus and pituitary, not suppression of GnRH activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progesterone rises after ovulation from the corpus luteum; theca cells produce androstenedione during the follicular phase.

questions.stem: During an in vitro fertilization procedure, an oocyte is retrieved shortly after its release from a dominant follicle. Before any contact with sperm, this oocyte is in which stage of meiosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arrested in prophase of meiosis I

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arrested in metaphase of meiosis I

choices.label: C
choices.text: Arrested in metaphase of meiosis II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Completed meiosis II with a mature ovum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Actively undergoing cleavage divisions

explanation.summary: Ovulation releases a secondary oocyte arrested in metaphase II, which completes meiosis II only if fertilization occurs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ovulation is the release of a secondary oocyte arrested in metaphase II from the dominant follicle. Meiosis II is completed only if fertilization occurs, after which the zygote undergoes cleavage and develops into a blastocyst.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Prophase I arrest describes the primary oocyte within primordial follicles, before the LH surge causes completion of meiosis I.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The LH surge causes the primary oocyte to complete meiosis I before ovulation; the released cell has passed this stage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meiosis II is completed only after fertilization, which has not occurred in this oocyte.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cleavage occurs in the zygote after fertilization, not in an unfertilized oocyte.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman with regular 28-day cycles develops sudden right lower-quadrant pain on day 14 of her cycle. The pain is unilateral, moderate, and resolves over the next day without intervention. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her pain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Breakdown and shedding of the functional endometrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Regression of the corpus luteum into a corpus albicans

choices.label: C
choices.text: Follicular rupture with limited bleeding irritating the peritoneum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trophoblast invasion of the secretory endometrium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Atresia of the nondominant follicles in the recruited cohort

explanation.summary: Mittelschmerz is unilateral lower-abdominal pain from peritoneal irritation caused by follicular rupture and limited bleeding at ovulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Midcycle unilateral lower-abdominal pain in a woman with regular cycles is characteristic of mittelschmerz. It results from peritoneal irritation associated with follicular rupture and limited bleeding during ovulation, which occurs near day 14 of a 28-day cycle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Endometrial shedding causes menstruation beginning on day 1 of the cycle, not midcycle unilateral pain.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Corpus luteum regression occurs late in the luteal phase and precedes menstruation; it does not cause midcycle pain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trophoblast invasion accompanies implantation after fertilization and is not a midcycle event in this patient.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Atresia of nondominant follicles occurs as FSH declines during the follicular phase and is not described as a cause of peritoneal pain.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman conceives during the current cycle. Three weeks after ovulation, her serum progesterone remains elevated and no menstruation has occurred. Which of the following best explains the continued progesterone secretion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: LH from the anterior pituitary continues to rise after implantation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Trophoblast-derived hCG maintains the corpus luteum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibin A stimulates luteal progesterone synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: The corpus albicans takes over steroid secretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sustained estradiol exerts positive feedback on the corpus luteum

explanation.summary: After implantation, trophoblast-derived hCG maintains the corpus luteum and its progesterone secretion during early pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: In a nonpregnant luteal phase, absence of hCG allows the corpus luteum to regress, ovarian steroids to fall, and menstruation to follow. When implantation occurs, trophoblast cells produce hCG, which maintains the corpus luteum and its progesterone secretion until placental steroid production becomes sufficient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Luteal progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A suppress gonadotropin secretion; pituitary LH does not rise to rescue the corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin A suppresses FSH secretion; it is a product of the corpus luteum, not a stimulus for progesterone synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The corpus albicans is the fibrotic remnant that forms after the corpus luteum's endocrine function ends; it does not secrete steroids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estradiol's positive feedback acts on the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary to generate the LH surge, not on the corpus luteum.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is on day 2 of her menstrual cycle. Compared with the late luteal phase of her previous cycle, her serum FSH concentration has risen. Which of the following best explains this rise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased inhibin B secretion from the new follicular cohort

choices.label: B
choices.text: Positive feedback from sustained high estradiol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreased negative feedback after regression of the corpus luteum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rising hCG secretion from the endometrium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased LH-receptor expression on granulosa cells

explanation.summary: Corpus luteum regression removes progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A negative feedback, allowing FSH to rise at the start of the follicular phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Regression of the previous cycle's corpus luteum decreases progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A. The resulting reduction in negative feedback on the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary allows FSH to rise, supporting growth of a new cohort of gonadotropin-responsive follicles.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibin B from developing follicles decreases FSH secretion; it does not cause FSH to rise.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sustained high estradiol occurs late in the follicular phase and generates the LH surge, not the early-cycle FSH rise.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hCG is produced by trophoblast cells only when implantation occurs, and menstruation indicates implantation did not occur.
whyWrongByChoice.E: FSH promotes LH-receptor expression in the dominant follicle during late follicular maturation; this is a downstream event, not the cause of the early FSH rise.

questions.stem: During the mid-follicular phase, rising estradiol and inhibin B cause serum FSH to decline, yet a single follicle continues maturing toward ovulation while the rest of the recruited cohort degenerates. Which of the following properties best explains why this follicle survives?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the most responsive to FSH within the cohort

choices.label: B
choices.text: It secretes inhibin A that stimulates its own granulosa cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: It contains an oocyte that has already completed meiosis I

choices.label: D
choices.text: It develops a vascularized granulosa-cell compartment

choices.label: E
choices.text: It escapes gonadotropin dependence at the antral stage

explanation.summary: As FSH declines under estradiol and inhibin B feedback, the follicle most responsive to FSH becomes dominant while less-responsive follicles undergo atresia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estradiol and inhibin B decrease FSH secretion during the follicular phase. As FSH declines, less-responsive follicles undergo atresia, while the follicle most responsive to FSH continues maturing as the dominant follicle; FSH also promotes LH-receptor expression in its granulosa cells during late maturation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Inhibin A from the dominant follicle contributes to FSH suppression at the pituitary; it is not described as a self-stimulating growth signal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The primary oocyte completes meiosis I only in response to the LH surge, just before ovulation, not at selection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The granulosa-cell compartment remains avascular; it is the theca that becomes vascularized.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antral follicles are gonadotropin dependent; dominance reflects superior FSH responsiveness, not independence from gonadotropins.

questions.stem: A reproductive physiologist studies a granulosa-cell hormone that rises as a cohort of follicles develops during the follicular phase and selectively decreases pituitary secretion of FSH without an equivalent effect on LH. Which of the following hormones is being studied?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhibin A

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibin B

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progesterone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation.summary: Inhibin B from granulosa cells of developing follicles selectively decreases FSH secretion during the follicular phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inhibin B is produced by granulosa cells of developing follicles during the follicular phase and selectively decreases FSH secretion. This selective FSH suppression contributes to atresia of less-responsive follicles and selection of the dominant follicle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibin A is produced by the dominant follicle late in the follicular phase and predominantly by the corpus luteum during the luteal phase, not by the developing cohort early on.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estradiol suppresses gonadotropin secretion broadly during most of the follicular phase rather than selectively targeting FSH.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progesterone is a corpus luteum product of the luteal phase, not a granulosa-cell hormone of the developing cohort.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG is produced by trophoblast cells after implantation and maintains the corpus luteum; it is not a granulosa-cell feedback hormone.

questions.stem: An endometrial biopsy obtained from a healthy 27-year-old woman on day 10 of her cycle shows regenerating glands and stroma of the functional layer with abundant mitotic figures. Which of the following hormones is primarily responsible for these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Progesterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Follicle-stimulating hormone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation.summary: Estradiol from developing follicles drives regeneration and proliferation of the functional endometrium during the proliferative phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Day 10 falls in the proliferative phase, which runs from the end of menstruation to ovulation. Estradiol produced by developing follicles stimulates regeneration and proliferation of the glandular epithelium and stroma of the functional endometrium and induces progesterone-receptor expression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Progesterone acts after ovulation, decreasing mitotic activity and producing secretory change; it does not drive proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LH acts on theca cells and triggers ovulation; it does not directly stimulate endometrial proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FSH acts on granulosa cells to support follicular maturation and estradiol synthesis; it is not the direct endometrial stimulus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG maintains the corpus luteum after implantation and has no role in a day-10 proliferative endometrium.

questions.stem: An endometrial biopsy from a healthy 33-year-old woman on day 22 of a 28-day cycle shows tortuous, actively secreting glands, stromal maturation, and markedly decreased mitotic activity. These changes are primarily produced by a hormone secreted from which of the following sources?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Granulosa cells of the dominant follicle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gonadotropes of the anterior pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lipid-rich cells of the corpus luteum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trophoblast cells of an implanting blastocyst

choices.label: E
choices.text: Theca cells of recruited antral follicles

explanation.summary: Progesterone from the corpus luteum transforms the estradiol-primed endometrium into secretory tissue during the secretory phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Day 22 is in the secretory phase. Progesterone from the corpus luteum, a highly vascular temporary endocrine structure whose lipid-rich cells synthesize progesterone and estradiol, decreases mitotic activity and produces tortuous secretory glands and stromal changes that make the endometrium receptive to implantation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Granulosa cells of the dominant follicle produce estradiol during the follicular phase, which drives proliferation rather than secretory change.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anterior-pituitary gonadotropes secrete LH and FSH, which act on the ovary, not directly on the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trophoblast cells secrete hCG after implantation; secretory transformation occurs whether or not implantation happens.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Theca cells produce androstenedione as an estradiol precursor; they are not the source of the secretory-phase hormone.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman requests combined oral contraceptive pills and asks how they prevent pregnancy so effectively. Which of the following best describes their primary mechanism of action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Suppressing gonadotropin secretion, preventing the LH surge and ovulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Accelerating atresia of the primordial follicle pool in both ovaries

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blocking completion of meiosis II after the oocyte is fertilized

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inducing early regression of the corpus luteum after ovulation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stimulating proliferation of the functional endometrial layer

explanation.summary: Combined oral contraceptives suppress gonadotropin secretion through negative feedback, preventing the LH surge required for ovulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Combined oral contraceptives act primarily through negative feedback that suppresses gonadotropin secretion, so the LH surge required for ovulation never occurs. The progestin component additionally thickens cervical mucus and reduces endometrial receptivity.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The finite follicle pool declines through atresia across the lifespan regardless of contraception; pills do not act by destroying the ovarian reserve.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Preventing pregnancy by these pills occurs upstream, at ovulation; they do not act by arresting meiosis after fertilization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Their mechanism prevents ovulation from happening, rather than causing luteal regression after an ovulation has occurred.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progestins reduce endometrial receptivity; stimulating endometrial proliferation is an estradiol effect of the normal cycle, not a contraceptive mechanism.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman asks whether her ovaries will keep producing new eggs if she delays childbearing. Which of the following statements about the ovarian follicle pool is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is established before birth and declines through atresia without replenishment

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is replenished each cycle by activation of newly formed primordial follicles

choices.label: C
choices.text: It expands during the follicular phase under the influence of FSH

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is maintained at a constant size until natural menopause occurs

choices.label: E
choices.text: It consists of secondary oocytes arrested in metaphase II from birth

explanation.summary: The ovarian reserve of about 1-2 million primary oocytes is established before birth and progressively declines through atresia, without replenishment.
explanation.whyCorrect: The follicle pool contains approximately 1-2 million primary oocytes at birth. This finite ovarian reserve is established before birth, is not replenished afterward, and progressively declines through atresia across the reproductive lifespan; only a small minority of activated follicles ultimately ovulate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Primordial follicles form during fetal development; no new primordial follicles are made after birth.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSH supports growth of already-recruited gonadotropin-responsive follicles; it does not enlarge the total follicle pool.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pool declines progressively through atresia throughout life; menopause reflects the loss of ovarian follicular activity, not a sudden drop from a constant reserve.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primordial follicles contain primary oocytes arrested in prophase I; metaphase II arrest describes the secondary oocyte formed just before ovulation.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has had no menstrual periods for the past 13 months. She is not pregnant, and her cycles were previously regular before becoming infrequent. Her amenorrhea is most likely due to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Persistent corpus luteum secretion of progesterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sustained trophoblast-derived hCG secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of ovarian follicular activity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Positive estradiol feedback on the pituitary

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased inhibin B secretion from developing follicles

explanation.summary: Natural menopause is recognized retrospectively after 12 consecutive months without menstruation due to loss of ovarian follicular activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: This woman has gone more than 12 consecutive months without menstruation, which retrospectively establishes natural menopause. The underlying cause is loss of ovarian follicular activity, since the finite follicle pool declines through atresia across the reproductive lifespan and is not replenished.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Without hCG, the corpus luteum regresses at the end of each luteal phase; it does not persist for over a year.
whyWrongByChoice.B: hCG is produced by trophoblast cells only after implantation, and this patient is not pregnant.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Positive estradiol feedback occurs late in the follicular phase of an ovulatory cycle and generates the LH surge; it does not explain prolonged amenorrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibin B comes from granulosa cells of developing follicles; in menopause follicular activity is lost, and inhibin B does not cause amenorrhea.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with regular cycles conceives naturally this month. Fertilization of the released secondary oocyte most likely occurred at which of the following sites?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Within the dominant ovarian follicle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Within the uterine tube

choices.label: C
choices.text: Within the uterine endometrial cavity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Within the cervical canal

choices.label: E
choices.text: On the surface of the ovary

explanation.summary: The ovulated secondary oocyte is captured by the uterine tube, where fertilization may occur.
explanation.whyCorrect: At ovulation, the secondary oocyte released from the dominant follicle is captured by the uterine tube and transported toward the uterus. Fertilization may occur within the uterine tube; the resulting zygote then undergoes cleavage as it develops into a blastocyst.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The oocyte leaves the follicle at ovulation; sperm do not fertilize the oocyte inside an intact follicle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The conceptus reaches the uterine cavity as a developing conceptus for implantation; fertilization occurs earlier, in the uterine tube.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The cervical canal is a passageway for sperm, not the site where the oocyte is fertilized.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The oocyte is captured by the uterine tube after release; fertilization is not described as occurring on the ovarian surface.

questions.stem: A secondary oocyte is fertilized in the uterine tube. Which of the following sequences best describes the development of the conceptus from fertilization to implantation in the endometrium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Zygote, then blastocyst, then cleavage, then implantation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastocyst, then cleavage, then zygote, then implantation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cleavage, then zygote, then blastocyst, then implantation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Zygote, then cleavage, then blastocyst, then implantation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Zygote, then cleavage, then implantation, then blastocyst

explanation.summary: Fertilization produces a zygote that undergoes cleavage, develops into a blastocyst, and may then implant in the endometrium.
explanation.whyCorrect: When fertilization occurs, the secondary oocyte completes meiosis II and the resulting zygote undergoes cleavage divisions. The conceptus develops into a blastocyst, and it is the blastocyst that may implant in the endometrium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The blastocyst forms as a result of cleavage; it cannot precede the cleavage divisions.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The zygote is the first stage after fertilization; a blastocyst does not exist before the zygote.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cleavage refers to the divisions of the zygote, so the zygote must come first.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Implantation is carried out by the blastocyst, so the blastocyst stage must be reached before implantation.

questions.stem: Histologic examination of an ovary from a newborn girl shows numerous small follicles, each consisting of an oocyte surrounded by a single flattened layer of granulosa cells. The oocytes within these follicles are arrested in which stage of meiosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prophase of meiosis I

choices.label: B
choices.text: Metaphase of meiosis I

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anaphase of meiosis I

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metaphase of meiosis II

choices.label: E
choices.text: Completion of meiosis II

explanation.summary: Primordial follicles contain primary oocytes arrested in prophase I of meiosis, surrounded by a flattened layer of granulosa cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Follicles with an oocyte surrounded by a single flattened granulosa layer are primordial follicles, which form during fetal development. Each contains a primary oocyte arrested in prophase I of meiosis, and approximately 1-2 million are present at birth.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Meiosis I is completed only in response to the LH surge, decades later in a follicle that reaches ovulation; there is no arrest at metaphase I in primordial follicles.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The oocyte remains arrested in prophase I; it does not progress to anaphase I until the LH surge permits completion of meiosis I.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metaphase II arrest describes the secondary oocyte formed just before ovulation, not the oocyte of a primordial follicle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Meiosis II is completed only if fertilization occurs, which is not applicable to fetal or newborn oocytes.

questions.stem: During the transition from a primordial to a primary follicle, the oocyte increases in size and the surrounding granulosa cells become cuboidal. Which additional structural feature develops at this stage to support interaction between the oocyte and its surrounding cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A fluid-filled antrum within the granulosa compartment

choices.label: B
choices.text: A vascularized outer theca layer

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proliferation of granulosa cells into multiple layers

choices.label: D
choices.text: LH-receptor expression on the granulosa cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gap junctions between the oocyte and granulosa cells

explanation.summary: In the primary follicle, gap junctions develop between the oocyte and its cuboidal granulosa cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The primary follicle is defined by an enlarging primary oocyte surrounded by a cuboidal layer of granulosa cells. At this stage, gap junctions develop between the oocyte and the granulosa cells, providing a route of communication that supports the oocyte.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The antrum forms later, in tertiary follicles, under FSH stimulation once follicles become gonadotropin dependent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The theca develops and becomes vascularized at the secondary-follicle stage, not during the primordial-to-primary transition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Granulosa cells proliferate into multiple layers in secondary follicles; the primary follicle has a single cuboidal layer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FSH promotes LH-receptor expression in granulosa cells of the dominant follicle during late follicular maturation, far beyond the primary stage.

questions.stem: A secondary ovarian follicle with multiple granulosa-cell layers and a distinct outer theca is examined microscopically. Which of the following best describes the distribution of its blood supply?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both the granulosa and theca layers are vascularized

choices.label: B
choices.text: The theca is vascularized and the granulosa compartment is avascular

choices.label: C
choices.text: The granulosa layer is vascularized and the theca is avascular

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither layer acquires blood vessels until after ovulation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Blood vessels reach the oocyte directly through the granulosa layer

explanation.summary: In the secondary follicle, the theca becomes vascularized while the granulosa-cell compartment remains avascular.
explanation.whyCorrect: As the secondary follicle develops, granulosa cells proliferate into multiple layers and a distinct outer theca forms. The theca becomes vascularized, whereas the granulosa-cell compartment remains avascular.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The granulosa compartment remains avascular during follicular development; only the theca acquires vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This reverses the actual arrangement; it is the theca, not the granulosa, that is vascularized.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The theca becomes vascularized during the secondary-follicle stage, well before ovulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vessels do not penetrate the avascular granulosa compartment to reach the oocyte.

questions.stem: In an experimental model, ovarian tissue develops with essentially no exposure to LH or FSH. Follicular development in this tissue would most likely proceed normally through which of the following stages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only the primordial-follicle stage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only the primary-follicle stage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Through the mid-secondary stage

choices.label: D
choices.text: Through antrum formation in tertiary follicles

choices.label: E
choices.text: Through maturation of a preovulatory follicle

explanation.summary: Follicular development through the mid-secondary stage is independent of gonadotropin secretion; later maturation requires gonadotropins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Early folliculogenesis is independent of gonadotropins: development through the mid-secondary stage does not require gonadotropin secretion. Beyond that point, follicles become gonadotropin dependent, and FSH is needed for granulosa-cell proliferation, antrum formation, and continued maturation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Activation of primordial follicles and progression through the primary stage do not require gonadotropins, so development would not stop at the primordial stage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Primary follicles progress to secondary follicles without gonadotropin stimulation, so development continues beyond the primary stage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antrum formation in tertiary follicles requires FSH, which is absent in this model.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Maturation of a dominant preovulatory follicle requires gonadotropin stimulation and could not occur without LH and FSH.

questions.stem: A recruited ovarian follicle has just become gonadotropin dependent, and FSH is stimulating its granulosa cells. Which characteristic structural change defines its progression to the tertiary-follicle stage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arrest of the oocyte in prophase of meiosis I

choices.label: B
choices.text: Development of gap junctions with the oocyte

choices.label: C
choices.text: First appearance of the outer theca layer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Formation of a fluid-filled antrum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Luteinization of granulosa and theca cells

explanation.summary: In gonadotropin-dependent tertiary follicles, FSH supports granulosa-cell proliferation and formation of the fluid-filled antrum.
explanation.whyCorrect: As follicles become gonadotropin dependent, FSH supports granulosa-cell proliferation and formation of the fluid-filled antrum, the defining feature of the tertiary (antral) follicle. One antral follicle is then selected as the dominant follicle and matures toward ovulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Prophase I arrest is established in primordial follicles during fetal development, not at the tertiary stage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gap junctions between the oocyte and granulosa cells develop at the primary-follicle stage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The distinct outer theca first develops in secondary follicles, before gonadotropin dependence.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Luteinization occurs after ovulation, when remaining granulosa and theca cells form the corpus luteum.

questions.stem: On day 12 of a 28-day cycle, the dominant follicle is uniquely prepared to respond to the impending midcycle gonadotropin surge with rupture and oocyte release. Which FSH-dependent change during late follicular maturation most directly confers this capacity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Induction of LH receptors on its granulosa cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of its theca cells into lipid-rich luteal cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Restoration of gonadotropin-independent growth

choices.label: D
choices.text: Selective secretion of inhibin B by its granulosa cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Completion of meiosis II by its oocyte

explanation.summary: During late follicular maturation, FSH promotes LH-receptor expression in granulosa cells of the dominant follicle, enabling its response to the LH surge.
explanation.whyCorrect: During late follicular maturation, FSH promotes LH-receptor expression in the granulosa cells of the dominant follicle. This allows the LH surge to activate receptors in the dominant preovulatory follicle and initiate the biochemical and structural changes that culminate in follicular rupture.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Luteinization of granulosa and theca cells occurs after ovulation, when the corpus luteum forms, not before the surge.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antral follicles remain gonadotropin dependent; the dominant follicle does not regain gonadotropin-independent growth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B is a feedback hormone that decreases FSH secretion; it does not equip the follicle to respond to the LH surge.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Meiosis II is completed only if fertilization occurs; before ovulation the LH surge causes completion of meiosis I.

questions.stem: Shortly after the midcycle LH surge, the wall of the dominant preovulatory follicle weakens and then ruptures, releasing the secondary oocyte. Which of the following processes most directly enables the follicular wall to rupture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apoptosis of the entire granulosa-cell layer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rapid regression of the corpus luteum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Traction on the follicle by the uterine tube

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of the blood supply to the outer theca

choices.label: E
choices.text: Proteolytic remodeling of the follicular wall

explanation.summary: The LH surge initiates coordinated changes including proteolytic remodeling of the follicular wall, culminating in rupture and oocyte release.
explanation.whyCorrect: The LH surge activates receptors in the dominant preovulatory follicle and initiates coordinated biochemical and structural changes, including proteolytic remodeling of the follicular wall. These changes culminate in follicular rupture and release of the secondary oocyte.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Granulosa cells are not destroyed at ovulation; those remaining in the ruptured follicle luteinize to form the corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The corpus luteum does not yet exist at the moment of ovulation; it forms from the follicle after rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The uterine tube captures the released oocyte; it does not mechanically pull the follicle open.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ovulation results from enzymatic remodeling of the wall, not from ischemia of the vascularized theca.

questions.stem: Two days after ovulation, a highly vascular temporary endocrine structure has formed within the ruptured follicle and is secreting progesterone and estradiol. This structure is derived from which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Trophoblast cells invading from an implanted blastocyst

choices.label: B
choices.text: Luteinized granulosa and theca cells of the ruptured follicle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fibrotic tissue remaining from a prior corpus albicans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Granulosa cells of atretic follicles in the recruited cohort

choices.label: E
choices.text: Regenerating stromal cells of the functional endometrium

explanation.summary: The corpus luteum forms from luteinized granulosa and theca cells remaining in the follicle after release of the secondary oocyte.
explanation.whyCorrect: After ovulation, the granulosa and theca cells remaining in the ruptured follicle luteinize to form the corpus luteum, or yellow body. This highly vascular temporary endocrine structure contains lipid-rich cells that synthesize progesterone and estradiol during the luteal phase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Trophoblast cells produce hCG after implantation; they do not form the corpus luteum, which arises from ovarian follicle cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The corpus albicans is the fibrotic end product of corpus luteum regression, not the origin of a new corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The other follicles of the recruited cohort undergo atresia; only the ruptured dominant follicle gives rise to the corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometrial stroma belongs to the uterus and responds to ovarian steroids; it does not form ovarian endocrine structures.

questions.stem: An ovary removed from a 45-year-old woman with regular menstrual cycles contains several small, white, fibrotic structures scattered through the cortex. These structures most likely represent which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Primordial follicles that underwent atresia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dominant follicles arrested before rupture

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implantation sites from prior pregnancies

choices.label: D
choices.text: Corpora lutea that have regressed

choices.label: E
choices.text: Theca layers of persistent antral follicles

explanation.summary: After its endocrine function ends, the corpus luteum regresses and forms the fibrotic corpus albicans.
explanation.whyCorrect: After the corpus luteum's endocrine function ends, it regresses and forms the fibrotic corpus albicans. In a woman with years of ovulatory cycles, multiple white fibrotic remnants of prior corpora lutea are an expected finding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atresia progressively depletes the follicle pool, but the corpus albicans is specifically the fibrotic remnant of a regressed corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A dominant follicle that reaches the preovulatory stage ruptures in response to the LH surge; arrested intact follicles are not the described fibrotic scars.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Implantation occurs in the uterine endometrium, not in the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vascularized theca is a layer of the developing follicle; it does not persist as a discrete white fibrotic body.

questions.stem: A healthy 28-year-old woman is on day 21 of a 28-day cycle. In addition to progesterone and estradiol, her corpus luteum secretes a peptide hormone that contributes to suppression of FSH secretion during this phase. Which of the following is that hormone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhibin A

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibin B

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone

explanation.summary: Inhibin A is produced predominantly by the corpus luteum during the luteal phase and contributes to suppression of FSH secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inhibin A is produced by the dominant follicle late in the follicular phase and predominantly by the corpus luteum during the luteal phase. Together with progesterone and estradiol, it suppresses gonadotropin secretion, contributing specifically to suppression of FSH.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Inhibin B comes from granulosa cells of developing follicles during the follicular phase, not from the corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG is a trophoblast product that appears only if implantation occurs; it maintains the corpus luteum rather than being secreted by it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LH is an anterior-pituitary hormone that supports the corpus luteum; it is not a luteal secretory product.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GnRH is a hypothalamic peptide that stimulates gonadotropes; it is not produced by the corpus luteum.

questions.stem: A hypothalamic peptide released in pulsatile fashion stimulates gonadotropes of the anterior pituitary to secrete LH and FSH, with a pulse frequency that varies with age, reproductive state, and phase of the menstrual cycle. This peptide reaches the gonadotropes by which of the following routes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct axonal transport into the anterior pituitary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Systemic arterial circulation after ovarian secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hypophyseal-portal circulation from the hypothalamus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Local diffusion from the posterior pituitary

choices.label: E
choices.text: Release from luteal cells into the ovarian veins

explanation.summary: GnRH travels from the hypothalamus through the hypophyseal-portal circulation to reach receptors on anterior-pituitary gonadotropes.
explanation.whyCorrect: GnRH is released from the hypothalamus into the hypophyseal-portal circulation and binds to receptors on anterior-pituitary gonadotropes, stimulating LH and FSH secretion. Its pulsatile release pattern varies with age, reproductive state, and cycle phase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GnRH is delivered through portal blood vessels, not by axons projecting into the anterior pituitary.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH originates in the hypothalamus, not the ovary, and uses the local portal system rather than the systemic circulation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GnRH acts on the anterior pituitary via the portal circulation; it is not released from the posterior pituitary.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Luteal cells secrete progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A; they are not the source of GnRH.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman is on day 20 of her cycle. A pregnancy test is negative. Continued secretion of progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A by her corpus luteum during this phase is supported primarily by which of the following hormones?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Follicle-stimulating hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibin B

choices.label: E
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

explanation.summary: During a nonpregnant luteal phase, LH supports corpus luteum secretion of progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A.
explanation.whyCorrect: In a nonpregnant luteal phase, LH supports corpus luteum secretion of progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A. Only if implantation occurs does trophoblast-derived hCG take over maintenance of the corpus luteum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: FSH acts on granulosa cells during follicular development; it is not the hormone supporting the corpus luteum, and luteal products suppress its secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: hCG appears only after implantation; this patient's pregnancy test is negative, so hCG is absent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estradiol is one of the corpus luteum's own products, not the pituitary support signal for luteal secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B is a follicular-phase granulosa-cell hormone that decreases FSH; it does not sustain the corpus luteum.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with regular 28-day cycles did not conceive this cycle. On day 28, breakdown and shedding of the functional endometrium begins. Which of the following most directly initiates this process?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A midcycle surge in LH secretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: A fall in progesterone and estradiol after luteal regression

choices.label: C
choices.text: A rise in FSH acting on the endometrial glands

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increasing inhibin B from the new follicular cohort

choices.label: E
choices.text: Invasion of the endometrium by trophoblast cells

explanation.summary: Corpus luteum regression withdraws progesterone and estradiol support from the endometrium, causing breakdown and shedding of the functional layer.
explanation.whyCorrect: When implantation does not occur, hCG remains absent and the corpus luteum regresses, so progesterone and estradiol concentrations decline. Loss of this hormonal support causes breakdown and shedding of the functional endometrium, which is menstruation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The LH surge occurs at midcycle and triggers ovulation; it is not the signal for endometrial shedding two weeks later.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSH acts on ovarian granulosa cells; it does not act on endometrial glands to cause menstruation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B regulates pituitary FSH secretion; it has no described role in initiating endometrial breakdown.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trophoblast invasion occurs only when a blastocyst implants, which prevents menstruation rather than causing it.

questions.stem: Microscopic examination of menstrual effluent from a healthy 26-year-old woman on day 2 of her cycle would most likely show blood together with which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Luteinized granulosa cells shed from the corpus luteum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Atretic follicles containing degenerating primary oocytes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fragments of endometrial glands and stroma with inflammatory cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trophoblast cells with fragments of chorionic tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Secondary oocytes arrested in metaphase of meiosis II

explanation.summary: Menstrual tissue contains blood, fragments of endometrial glands and stroma, and inflammatory cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: During the menstrual phase, regression of the corpus luteum withdraws progesterone and estradiol support, and the functional endometrium breaks down and is shed. The resulting menstrual tissue contains blood, fragments of endometrial glands and stroma, and inflammatory cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The corpus luteum regresses within the ovary to form the corpus albicans; its cells are not shed through the uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Atresia occurs within the ovary; degenerating follicles do not appear in menstrual effluent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trophoblast and chorionic tissue exist only in pregnancy, and menstruation indicates implantation did not occur.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The ovulated secondary oocyte is captured by the uterine tube; oocytes are not a component of menstrual tissue.

questions.stem: In an experimental study, endometrial tissue is exposed to progesterone without any prior estradiol exposure, and secretory transformation fails to occur. Prior estradiol exposure is most likely required because estradiol has which of the following effects on the endometrium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It converts stromal cells directly into secretory glands

choices.label: B
choices.text: It decreases mitotic activity in the glandular epithelium

choices.label: C
choices.text: It stimulates trophoblast invasion into the stroma

choices.label: D
choices.text: It induces expression of progesterone receptors

choices.label: E
choices.text: It transforms glands into a tortuous secretory pattern

explanation.summary: Estradiol induces progesterone-receptor expression in the endometrium, priming it so progesterone can produce secretory transformation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estradiol stimulates proliferation of the glandular epithelium and stroma of the functional endometrium and induces progesterone-receptor expression. Progesterone then acts on this estradiol-primed endometrium to produce secretory transformation; without estradiol priming, the tissue lacks the receptors needed to respond.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estradiol drives proliferation of glands and stroma; secretory differentiation of the glands is a progesterone effect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Decreased mitotic activity is produced by progesterone after ovulation, not by estradiol.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Trophoblast invasion follows blastocyst implantation and is not an estradiol effect on the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tortuous secretory glands are produced by progesterone acting on the primed endometrium, not by estradiol itself.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman is in the sixth week of pregnancy. In addition to promoting secretory differentiation and maintenance of the endometrium, progesterone supports the early pregnancy through which of the following actions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maintaining uterine quiescence

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stimulating proliferation of the functional endometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Generating a preovulatory LH surge

choices.label: D
choices.text: Triggering proteolytic rupture of ovarian follicles

choices.label: E
choices.text: Maintaining the corpus luteum after implantation

explanation.summary: Progesterone promotes secretory differentiation of the endometrium and helps maintain uterine quiescence.
explanation.whyCorrect: Progesterone from the corpus luteum promotes secretory differentiation and receptivity of the endometrium and supports the early conceptus before the placental circulation is established. It also helps maintain uterine quiescence, which supports continuation of the early pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Proliferation of the functional endometrium is an estradiol effect during the proliferative phase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The LH surge is generated by sustained high estradiol through positive feedback; progesterone does not produce it, and ovulation is not a goal in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Follicular rupture is initiated by the LH surge acting on the dominant follicle, not by progesterone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The corpus luteum is maintained after implantation by trophoblast-derived hCG, not by its own progesterone.

questions.stem: A blastocyst implants successfully, and trophoblast cells invade the endometrium. The placenta that subsequently develops is derived from which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fetal chorionic tissue only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maternal decidua only

choices.label: C
choices.text: The corpus luteum and fetal chorionic tissue

choices.label: D
choices.text: The maternal decidua and the corpus luteum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fetal chorionic tissue and the maternal decidua

explanation.summary: After implantation, the placenta develops from fetal chorionic tissue together with the maternal decidua.
explanation.whyCorrect: If a blastocyst implants, trophoblast cells invade the endometrium, and the placenta develops from fetal chorionic tissue and the maternal decidua. Once placental steroid production becomes sufficient, the corpus luteum is no longer needed for steroid support of the pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The placenta is not purely fetal; the maternal decidua contributes as well.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The placenta is not purely maternal; fetal chorionic tissue is an essential component.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The corpus luteum is an ovarian structure that supports early pregnancy hormonally; it does not become part of the placenta.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The fetal contribution comes from chorionic tissue, and the corpus luteum contributes no placental tissue.

questions.stem: A healthy 24-year-old woman tracks her cycles for a year and finds that they vary in length from 26 to 33 days. Variation in her overall cycle length is best attributed to variation in the duration of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The luteal phase

choices.label: B
choices.text: The follicular phase

choices.label: C
choices.text: The secretory phase

choices.label: D
choices.text: The menstrual phase

choices.label: E
choices.text: The process of follicular rupture

explanation.summary: Ovulation occurs near day 14 of a representative 28-day cycle, but its timing varies because follicular-phase duration varies.
explanation.whyCorrect: In a representative 28-day cycle, ovulation occurs near day 14, but its timing varies among cycles because the duration of the follicular phase varies. Differences in follicular-phase length therefore account for differences in overall cycle length.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The luteal phase runs from ovulation to the next menstruation and is not identified as the source of cycle-length variability.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The secretory phase corresponds to the luteal phase in the uterus; variability arises before ovulation, in the follicular phase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The menstrual phase is the shedding of the functional endometrium at the start of the cycle, not the described source of variable cycle length.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Follicular rupture is the brief event of ovulation itself, not a phase whose duration determines cycle length.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman undergoing in vitro fertilization receives daily injections of exogenous gonadotropins. Unlike her natural cycles, in which a single dominant follicle matures while the rest of the cohort degenerates, this cycle produces many mature follicles simultaneously. Which of the following best explains the difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exogenous gonadotropins increase the number of primordial follicles formed in the ovary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exogenous gonadotropins make antral follicles independent of gonadotropin stimulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exogenous gonadotropins sustain multiple follicles despite feedback from rising estradiol and inhibin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exogenous gonadotropins prevent estradiol from exerting positive feedback at midcycle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Exogenous gonadotropins restore development in follicles that already underwent atresia

explanation.summary: During controlled ovarian stimulation, exogenous gonadotropins support simultaneous development of multiple follicles despite endogenous negative feedback from rising estradiol and inhibin.
explanation.whyCorrect: In a natural cycle, rising estradiol and inhibin B suppress FSH, so less-responsive follicles undergo atresia and only the most FSH-responsive follicle survives as the dominant follicle. Exogenous gonadotropins bypass this bottleneck: they maintain gonadotropin support of the whole cohort despite endogenous negative feedback, so multiple follicles develop and their oocytes can be retrieved for fertilization in vitro.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Primordial follicles form during fetal development, and the ovarian reserve is not replenished after birth; no drug increases their number.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antral follicles remain gonadotropin dependent; stimulation supplies more gonadotropin rather than removing the requirement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Multiple-follicle development results from sustained gonadotropin support, not from blocking midcycle positive feedback.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Atresia is degeneration of the follicle; gonadotropins support still-viable follicles rather than reviving degenerated ones.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman starts a combined oral contraceptive. Beyond suppressing gonadotropin secretion and preventing the LH surge, the progestin component contributes to contraceptive efficacy by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increasing GnRH pulse frequency at the hypothalamus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Promoting proliferation of the functional endometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stimulating corpus luteum formation without ovulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thickening cervical mucus and reducing endometrial receptivity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enhancing FSH-driven recruitment of follicular cohorts

explanation.summary: The progestin component of combined oral contraceptives thickens cervical mucus and reduces endometrial receptivity, adding to the primary anovulatory effect.
explanation.whyCorrect: Combined oral contraceptives primarily prevent ovulation by suppressing gonadotropin secretion through negative feedback, so the LH surge never occurs. In addition, the progestin component thickens cervical mucus and reduces endometrial receptivity, providing further barriers to fertilization and implantation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Combined oral contraceptives suppress the GnRH-gonadotropin axis through negative feedback; they do not increase GnRH pulse activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endometrial proliferation is an estradiol effect of the normal cycle; progestins reduce endometrial receptivity rather than building it up.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The corpus luteum forms only from a follicle that has ovulated, and these pills prevent ovulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Suppressed gonadotropin secretion reduces, rather than enhances, gonadotropin-driven follicular development.

questions.stem: A dominant follicle ruptures and releases a secondary oocyte during a woman's current menstrual cycle. Development of this follicle from the primordial stage most likely began at which of the following times?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Months before the cycle in which ovulation occurred

choices.label: B
choices.text: On day 1 of the current cycle, when FSH began to rise

choices.label: C
choices.text: At the midpoint of the immediately preceding luteal phase

choices.label: D
choices.text: At the moment of the current midcycle LH surge

choices.label: E
choices.text: During the proliferative phase of the current cycle

explanation.summary: Development of a follicle that ultimately ovulates begins months before the ovulatory cycle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Progression from a primordial follicle to a preovulatory follicle is a prolonged process: development of a follicle that ultimately ovulates begins months before the cycle in which ovulation occurs. Early stages proceed independently of gonadotropins, and only the final gonadotropin-dependent maturation takes place within the ovulatory cycle itself.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The early-cycle FSH rise recruits a cohort of already-developed gonadotropin-responsive follicles; it does not initiate development from the primordial stage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The follicle destined to ovulate began developing long before the previous luteal phase, not within it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The LH surge acts on a fully mature preovulatory follicle to trigger ovulation; it is the end of the process, not its start.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The proliferative phase spans only the current cycle's follicular development; primordial-stage activation occurred months earlier.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old girl is brought to the clinic because she has never menstruated. For the past 5 months she has had severe lower abdominal pain that recurs roughly every 4 weeks and resolves after a few days. Breast development is Tanner stage 5, and pubic hair is normal for age. Pelvic examination shows a bulging, bluish membrane at the vaginal introitus, and ultrasound demonstrates blood distending the vagina. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Imperforate hymen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mullerian agenesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turner syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea

choices.label: E
choices.text: Asherman syndrome

explanation.summary: Primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain and normal secondary sexual characteristics points to an outflow tract obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Outflow tract disorders such as imperforate hymen prevent egress of menstrual blood despite normal hormonal cycling, so patients develop cyclic pain with hematocolpos (blood accumulating in the vagina). The bulging bluish membrane at the introitus is the obstructing hymen itself. Normal breast development confirms estrogen exposure, so the HPO axis is intact.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Mullerian agenesis causes an absent uterus (with or without upper vagina), so there is no cyclic endometrial shedding to accumulate and no cyclic pain or hematocolpos.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Turner syndrome causes primary amenorrhea from absent functional ovarian tissue, with delayed or incomplete puberty rather than Tanner 5 breasts and cyclic pain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea suppresses GnRH and estrogen output; it does not produce cyclic pain or blood trapped behind an obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Asherman syndrome is an acquired cause of secondary amenorrhea from intrauterine adhesions after instrumentation, not a congenital cause of primary amenorrhea.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman presents because her previously regular menses have been absent for 4 months. She takes no medications and reports no weight change. She states that pregnancy is "impossible" because she and her partner use condoms consistently. Which of the following is the most appropriate first step in evaluation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Serum or urine beta-hCG

choices.label: B
choices.text: Serum FSH and estradiol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum TSH

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pelvic ultrasound

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pituitary MRI

explanation.summary: Pregnancy is the first consideration in any reproductive-aged patient with secondary amenorrhea.
explanation.whyCorrect: Absence of menses for 3 or more months in a woman with previously regular cycles is secondary amenorrhea, and pregnancy must be excluded before any further workup. History alone cannot reliably exclude pregnancy, so beta-hCG testing is performed even when the patient reports pregnancy is unlikely.
