whyWrongByChoice.A: 21-hydroxylase deficiency is a form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia associated with androgen excess and precocious changes, not this triad of delayed puberty with hypertension and hypokalemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aromatase converts androgens to estrogens in peripheral tissues; its deficiency does not explain hypertension with hypokalemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 5-alpha-reductase acts on peripheral androgen conversion and does not produce this combination of blood pressure and electrolyte abnormalities.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This enzyme is not the steroidogenic defect the lecture ties to delayed puberty with hypertension and hypokalemia; CYP17A1 deficiency is.

questions.stem: A pediatrician is teaching medical students about disorders of pubertal timing. Development of secondary sex characteristics is considered precocious when it begins before which of the following ages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 7 years in females; 8 years in males

choices.label: B
choices.text: 8 years in females; 9 years in males

choices.label: C
choices.text: 9 years in females; 10 years in males

choices.label: D
choices.text: 8 years in both females and males

choices.label: E
choices.text: 10 years in females; 11 years in males

explanation.summary: Precocious puberty is secondary sex characteristic development before age 8 in females or age 9 in males.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines precocious puberty as development of secondary sex characteristics before age 8 years in females or age 9 years in males. Breast development in females and testicular enlargement in males are the key signs of early HPG-axis activation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These cutoffs are one year too early; development at age 7 in a girl or 8 in a boy already meets the definition of precocious puberty.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These cutoffs are one year too late; a 9-year-old girl or 10-year-old boy with new secondary sex characteristics is within the defined limits.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The thresholds differ by sex; males are given an extra year, with 9 years as the male cutoff.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Development beginning at 9 in a girl or 10 in a boy is not precocious by definition; these ages are too late to serve as cutoffs.

questions.stem: The mother of a healthy girl asks at what age the absence of any breast development would warrant an evaluation for delayed puberty. Absence of breast development by which of the following ages defines delayed puberty in females?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 11 years

choices.label: B
choices.text: 12 years

choices.label: C
choices.text: 13 years

choices.label: D
choices.text: 14 years

choices.label: E
choices.text: 15 years

explanation.summary: Delayed puberty in females is absence of breast development by age 13 years.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines delayed puberty as absence of breast development by age 13 years in females or absence of testicular enlargement by age 14 years in males. Breast development is the marker used in girls because it reflects estradiol production from HPG-axis activation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Age 11 is within the normal range of pubertal timing; absent breast development at this age does not yet meet the definition.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Age 12 is still within normal variation; the defined female cutoff is one year later.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Age 14 is the male cutoff, defined by absence of testicular enlargement, not the female threshold.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Waiting until age 15 would delay recognition; the female definition is met two years earlier.

questions.stem: A healthy 6-year-old girl has a quiescent hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, yet low-level estrogenic activity can still occur in some of her tissues. Which of the following best explains this phenomenon?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct secretion of estradiol by the adrenal zona reticularis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aromatization of adrenal androgen precursors in peripheral tissues

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adrenal androgen stimulation of ovarian granulosa-cell estradiol secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Conversion of DHEAS to estradiol within the adrenal medulla

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adrenal progesterone secretion with conversion to estradiol in the ovary

explanation.summary: Before gonadarche, weak adrenal androgen precursors are converted to estrogens in peripheral tissues that express aromatase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Before gonadarche, the adrenal cortex produces weak androgen precursors including DHEA, DHEAS, and androstenedione. These precursors circulate to peripheral tissues, where they may be converted to more potent androgens or, in tissues that express aromatase, to estrogens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The zona reticularis produces androgen precursors such as DHEA and DHEAS, not estradiol itself.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Substantial ovarian estradiol production requires gonadotropin stimulation after HPG-axis activation, which has not occurred in this prepubertal child.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Steroid conversion of adrenal precursors to estrogens occurs in peripheral aromatase-expressing tissues, not in the adrenal medulla.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pathway to estrogenic activity before gonadarche runs through peripheral aromatization of androgen precursors, not through ovarian conversion of adrenal progesterone.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old girl is brought in for a well-child visit. Her mother reports that a few coarse, dark hairs appeared on the mons pubis over the past month, the first pubic hair the girl has developed. Which of the following terms best describes this event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenarche

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gonadarche

choices.label: C
choices.text: Menarche

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pubarche

choices.label: E
choices.text: Precocious puberty

explanation.summary: Pubarche is the first appearance of pubic hair.
explanation.whyCorrect: The first appearance of pubic hair is called pubarche. It reflects androgen action, to which adrenal androgens contribute in both sexes, and at age 9 it falls within the normal range of pubertal timing for a girl.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenarche is the maturational increase in adrenal androgen production itself, not the appearance of pubic hair that may follow it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gonadarche is activation of the HPG axis with increased gonadal sex-steroid production, not the onset of pubic hair.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Menarche refers to the first menstrual period, which has not occurred here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Precocious puberty requires secondary sex characteristics before age 8 in a girl; this 9-year-old is within the normal range.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl is evaluated for early pubic hair and acne. On genital examination, there is substantial clitoral enlargement. Excess activity of which of the following hormone classes best explains the clitoral finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Androgens

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estrogens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progestins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolactin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gonadotropins

explanation.summary: Substantial clitoral enlargement in a girl indicates androgen excess.
explanation.whyCorrect: In females, estrogens promote maturation of the vulva and other reproductive tissues, but substantial clitoral enlargement may indicate androgen excess. Combined with pubic hair and acne, this examination finding points to excessive androgenic stimulation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Estrogens drive breast development and maturation of the vulva; they do not produce substantial clitoral enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Progestins are products of the corpus luteum after ovulation and do not cause clitoral enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolactin excess suppresses pulsatile GnRH secretion; it does not virilize the external genitalia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: LH and FSH act on the gonads; clitoral enlargement reflects the downstream androgen effect rather than gonadotropins themselves.

questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl is brought in because her menstrual periods, which began 8 months ago, occur unpredictably at intervals of 24 to 60 days. She is otherwise well, her examination is normal, and her pubertal development is appropriate. Which of the following best explains her irregular cycles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Failure of ovarian estradiol production

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of pulsatile GnRH secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inconsistent ovulation with inconsistent corpus luteum formation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hyperprolactinemia suppressing gonadotropin secretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Primary ovarian failure with elevated gonadotropins

explanation.summary: Ovulation may remain inconsistent after menarche, so corpus luteum formation and luteal progesterone secretion are also inconsistent.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture notes that ovulation may remain inconsistent after menarche, so cyclic corpus luteum formation and luteal progesterone secretion may also be inconsistent. In a recently menarchal girl with normal development and an otherwise normal evaluation, irregular cycles reflect this expected physiologic pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: She has appropriate pubertal development, which requires ongoing ovarian estradiol production; estradiol failure would present with absent or arrested development.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Loss of pulsatile GnRH secretion causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with pubertal arrest, not irregular cycling in a normally developing girl.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hyperprolactinemia suppresses pulsatile GnRH and would impair pubertal progression; nothing in this healthy girl suggests it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary ovarian failure produces low estradiol with elevated LH and FSH and arrested development, not normal puberty with irregular early cycles.

questions.stem: A 13-year-old boy at genital Tanner stage 2 asks when he is likely to grow the fastest. During which of the following periods does peak height velocity most likely occur in males?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Before any genital development begins

choices.label: B
choices.text: During genital Tanner stage 2

choices.label: C
choices.text: During genital Tanner stage 5

choices.label: D
choices.text: During genital Tanner stages 3-4

choices.label: E
choices.text: After genital Tanner stage 5 is complete

explanation.summary: Male peak height velocity generally occurs during genital Tanner stages 3-4.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peak height velocity generally occurs during genital Tanner stages 3-4 in males, later in the pubertal sequence than in females, whose peak occurs during breast Tanner stages 2-3. This boy at stage 2 can expect his fastest growth as he progresses through the next stages.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The growth spurt is driven by rising sex steroids together with the GH-IGF-1 axis, so it does not peak before pubertal development begins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Genital stage 2 corresponds to early puberty in males; peak height velocity comes later than in females, who peak at breast stages 2-3.
whyWrongByChoice.C: By genital stage 5, development is complete and growth is slowing as epiphyseal fusion approaches, past the peak.
whyWrongByChoice.E: After stage 5, epiphyseal growth-plate closure ends longitudinal growth rather than accelerating it.

questions.stem: On average, males gain more height during puberty than females. Which of the following best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Later onset and longer duration of the male growth spurt

choices.label: B
choices.text: Earlier onset of adrenarche in males than in females

choices.label: C
choices.text: Higher circulating estradiol concentrations in males during puberty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peak height velocity at an earlier Tanner stage in males

choices.label: E
choices.text: Faster epiphyseal fusion driven directly by testosterone in males

explanation.summary: The male growth spurt begins later and lasts longer, producing greater average pubertal height gain.
explanation.whyCorrect: The male pubertal growth spurt generally begins later and lasts longer than the female spurt, and this combination contributes to greater average pubertal height gain in males. Growth ends when estradiol-mediated epiphyseal fusion closes the growth plates.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Adrenarche is the maturational rise in adrenal androgens and is not described as occurring earlier in males or as the driver of their greater height gain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estradiol is the principal mediator of growth-plate maturation and fusion in both sexes; higher estradiol would end growth sooner, not extend it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Male peak height velocity occurs at genital stages 3-4, later in the sequence than the female peak at breast stages 2-3, not earlier.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Epiphyseal fusion is principally mediated by estradiol in both sexes, and faster fusion would reduce rather than increase total height gain.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl with early breast development is being evaluated. The physician wants an estimate of her skeletal maturation to compare with her chronologic age. Which of the following studies is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry of the lumbar spine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Magnetic resonance imaging of the knee

choices.label: C
choices.text: Computed tomography of the skull

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ultrasonography of the wrist

choices.label: E
choices.text: Radiography of the hand and wrist

explanation.summary: Bone age is assessed by radiography of the hand and wrist.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bone age, assessed by radiography of the hand and wrist, provides an estimate of skeletal maturation. Advanced bone age may accompany early sex-steroid exposure, as suspected in this girl, whereas delayed bone age may accompany delayed pubertal development.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DXA measures bone mineral density, not the skeletal maturation used to assign a bone age.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Knee MRI is not the described method for estimating skeletal maturation in pubertal evaluation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Skull CT does not provide the standardized hand-and-wrist assessment used for bone age.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ultrasonography of the wrist is not the modality described for bone-age determination; plain radiography is.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl has confirmed central precocious puberty with breast development and accelerated linear growth. Which of the following additional features would most strongly indicate the need for brain MRI?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Female sex

choices.label: B
choices.text: Advanced bone age on hand radiography

choices.label: C
choices.text: New morning headaches with vomiting

choices.label: D
choices.text: An LH-predominant response to GnRH stimulation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Height above the expected range for her family

explanation.summary: Brain MRI in central precocious puberty is particularly important in males, very young children, and patients with neurologic findings.
explanation.whyCorrect: Brain MRI is particularly important in males, very young children, patients with neurologic findings, or others with clinical concern for a central nervous system lesion. New morning headaches with vomiting are neurologic findings that raise concern for a CNS lesion such as a tumor and strongly indicate imaging.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An identifiable CNS cause is more likely in males than in females, so female sex by itself lowers rather than raises the imperative for imaging.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Advanced bone age is an expected accompaniment of early sex-steroid exposure in precocious puberty and does not specifically point to a CNS lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An LH-predominant pubertal response to GnRH stimulation establishes that the process is central; it is part of the diagnosis, not a specific red flag for a lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Accelerated growth and tall stature are typical of central precocious puberty itself and do not specifically indicate a CNS lesion.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl is evaluated for 6 months of progressive breast development followed by pubic hair, with accelerated linear growth. GnRH stimulation testing produces a pubertal, LH-predominant gonadotropin response. Which of the following processes underlies her condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autonomous estradiol secretion by an ovarian cyst

choices.label: B
choices.text: Early activation of pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exposure to an exogenous estrogen-containing product

choices.label: D
choices.text: A postzygotic activating GNAS variant in ovarian tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Excess androgen production by the adrenal cortex

explanation.summary: A pubertal, LH-predominant response to GnRH stimulation identifies central, GnRH-dependent precocious puberty.
explanation.whyCorrect: Central precocious puberty results from early activation of the HPG axis, and affected children show a pubertal gonadotropin response, particularly an LH-predominant response to GnRH stimulation. Her development also progresses in the typical sequence, beginning with breast development, which is characteristic of central disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An ovarian cyst producing estradiol causes peripheral precocious puberty, in which LH and FSH are low or suppressed rather than briskly responsive to GnRH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Exogenous estrogen exposure is GnRH-independent and suppresses gonadotropins, which is incompatible with a pubertal stimulation response.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An activating GNAS variant causes McCune-Albright syndrome with GnRH-independent steroid production and suppressed gonadotropins, plus bone and skin findings absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adrenal androgen excess produces androgenic changes and would not explain estrogen-driven breast development with a pubertal gonadotropin response.

questions.stem: An 11-year-old girl with idiopathic central precocious puberty diagnosed at age 6 has been treated with a long-acting GnRH agonist, and her physician now discontinues the drug because she has reached an appropriate developmental age. Which of the following is the expected outcome after discontinuation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Permanent suppression of LH and FSH secretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediate closure of the epiphyseal growth plates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conversion to a peripheral form of precocious puberty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resumption of HPG-axis activity with pubertal progression

choices.label: E
choices.text: A prepubertal state persisting until estrogen is prescribed

explanation.summary: Stopping a GnRH agonist at an appropriate developmental age allows HPG-axis activity to resume.
explanation.whyCorrect: GnRH-agonist therapy suppresses gonadotropins only while continuous receptor activation keeps gonadotropes desensitized. Treatment can be discontinued at an appropriate developmental age, allowing HPG-axis activity to resume so that puberty proceeds normally.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gonadotrope suppression depends on ongoing continuous receptor activation; it is not permanent once the agonist is withdrawn.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epiphyseal fusion is a gradual, estradiol-mediated process that occurs as puberty advances; it is not triggered abruptly by stopping the drug.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Her condition is GnRH-dependent; stopping the agonist restores central axis activity rather than creating GnRH-independent steroid production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Because her hypothalamus and pituitary are intact, endogenous pulsatile GnRH resumes on its own; exogenous estrogen is not required to initiate development.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old girl is evaluated for pubic hair, acne, and clitoral enlargement that have progressed over 6 months, with accelerated linear growth and advanced bone age. She has no breast development. Serum LH and FSH are low. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypothalamic hamartoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen-producing ovarian tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: McCune-Albright syndrome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Idiopathic central precocious puberty

explanation.summary: Virilizing (contrasexual) precocious changes with suppressed gonadotropins in a girl point to an adrenal androgen source such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peripheral precocious puberty produces sex steroids independent of pulsatile GnRH, so LH and FSH are low or suppressed, and the changes may be contrasexual. In this girl, androgenic findings including clitoral enlargement without any breast development indicate androgen rather than estrogen excess, and congenital adrenal hyperplasia is the listed peripheral cause that produces adrenal androgen excess.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A hypothalamic hamartoma causes central precocious puberty, which follows the typical estrogen-led sequence in girls, beginning with breast development, and shows pubertal rather than suppressed gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An estrogen-producing ovarian tumor causes isosexual changes with breast development, not virilization with clitoral enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: McCune-Albright syndrome classically combines peripheral precocious puberty with polyostotic fibrous dysplasia and cafe-au-lait macules, none of which are present.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Central precocious puberty is GnRH-dependent, produces breast development first in girls, and is not associated with suppressed LH and FSH.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy has 4 months of penile growth, pubic hair, and accelerated linear growth. Examination shows marked enlargement of the right testis; the left testis is prepubertal in size. Serum testosterone is markedly elevated, LH and FSH are suppressed, and serum hCG is undetectable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: hCG-secreting germ-cell tumor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leydig-cell tumor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Idiopathic central precocious puberty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Exogenous androgen exposure

explanation.summary: An androgen-producing Leydig-cell tumor causes peripheral precocious puberty in boys with asymmetric testicular enlargement, high testosterone, suppressed gonadotropins, and no hCG.
explanation.whyCorrect: In males, peripheral precocious puberty may result from androgen-producing Leydig-cell tumors. Autonomous testosterone production from the tumor suppresses LH and FSH, and the tumor itself accounts for enlargement of a single testis while the contralateral testis remains prepubertal without gonadotropin stimulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An hCG-secreting germ-cell tumor stimulates Leydig-cell testosterone production through LH receptors, but serum hCG would be elevated rather than undetectable.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Central precocious puberty produces gonadotropin-driven, bilateral testicular enlargement with a pubertal rather than suppressed gonadotropin pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia supplies androgens from the adrenal glands; it does not produce unilateral testicular enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Exogenous androgen exposure suppresses gonadotropins but provides no stimulus for testicular growth, so both testes would remain prepubertal.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl with McCune-Albright syndrome has progressive breast development and vaginal bleeding. Her physician trials a long-acting GnRH agonist, but after several months serum estradiol remains markedly elevated and pubertal changes continue to progress. Which of the following best explains the treatment failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The agonist dose was insufficient to desensitize her gonadotropes

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drug acted as a competitive GnRH-receptor antagonist

choices.label: C
choices.text: The initial stimulatory phase of the agonist has not yet resolved

choices.label: D
choices.text: Her estradiol arises from adrenal rather than ovarian tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Her ovarian estradiol production does not depend on gonadotropins

explanation.summary: Peripheral precocious puberty is GnRH-independent, so suppressing gonadotropins with a GnRH agonist does not stop autonomous sex-steroid production.
explanation.whyCorrect: McCune-Albright syndrome causes peripheral precocious puberty: a postzygotic activating GNAS variant drives constitutive Gs-alpha signaling and sex-steroid production independent of pulsatile GnRH. Because ovarian estradiol secretion is autonomous, desensitizing gonadotropes and lowering LH and FSH does not reduce it; treatment must instead target the source, using approaches such as medications that inhibit sex-steroid synthesis or receptor signaling.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dose adequacy is not the issue; even complete gonadotropin suppression cannot stop steroid production that never required gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH agonists act as receptor agonists that desensitize gonadotropes with continuous exposure; antagonism is not their mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The initial stimulatory phase is brief; months into therapy, persistent estradiol elevation reflects autonomous production, not ongoing agonist stimulation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: In females with McCune-Albright syndrome, the precocious estrogen excess arises from GnRH-independent ovarian steroid production, not from the adrenal glands.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old boy is evaluated for new pubic hair and adult-type body odor. His parents ask whether his 'puberty glands in the brain' have turned on early. Which of the following examination findings would most strongly indicate activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coarse pubic hair extending onto the mons

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adult-type axillary odor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Comedonal acne on the forehead

choices.label: D
choices.text: Testicular enlargement

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased penile length

explanation.summary: Testicular enlargement is the key sign of early HPG-axis activation in males.
explanation.whyCorrect: Breast development in females and testicular enlargement in males are the key signs of early HPG-axis activation. Testicular growth reflects gonadotropin stimulation of the testes, whereas the other findings can be produced by androgens from any source, including the adrenal glands.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenal androgens contribute to pubic-hair development in both sexes, so pubic hair alone can reflect adrenarche without HPG-axis activation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Body odor is an effect of adrenal androgens and can accompany isolated adrenarche.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sebaceous-gland activity and acne are adrenal androgen effects and do not require gonadotropin-driven testicular activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Androgens promote penile growth regardless of their source, so penile growth also occurs in GnRH-independent, peripheral processes.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy is evaluated for absent pubertal development. Serum testosterone is low, and LH and FSH are both markedly elevated. Karyotype analysis shows 47,XXY. Which of the following best explains the elevated gonadotropin concentrations in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Loss of sex-steroid negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autonomous gonadotropin secretion by a pituitary adenoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hyperprolactinemia stimulating gonadotropin release

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continuous rather than pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH secretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Excess adrenal DHEAS driving pituitary LH synthesis

explanation.summary: In primary hypogonadism, loss of sex-steroid negative feedback increases LH and FSH secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Klinefelter syndrome, classically 47,XXY, causes primary testicular failure. With low testosterone production, sex-steroid negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary is lost, so LH and FSH secretion rises, producing the pattern of low testosterone with elevated gonadotropins.

whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no pituitary tumor here; the gonadotropin rise is the physiologic response to failed testicular steroid output.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperprolactinemia suppresses pulsatile GnRH secretion and lowers LH and FSH; it does not stimulate them.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Continuous GnRH exposure desensitizes gonadotropes and suppresses LH and FSH, the opposite of this pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adrenal androgen precursors are weak androgens and are not described as stimulating pituitary LH synthesis.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old girl is evaluated for absent breast development, fatigue, cold intolerance, and weight gain. Examination shows a diffusely enlarged thyroid gland. Laboratory studies show a markedly elevated TSH, elevated prolactin, low estradiol, and low LH and FSH. Which of the following mechanisms best links her thyroid disease to her pubertal delay?

choices.label: A
choices.text: TSH directly inhibits ovarian estradiol synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Thyroid-hormone deficiency blocks peripheral aromatase activity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased TRH raises prolactin, which suppresses pulsatile GnRH secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elevated TSH desensitizes pituitary gonadotropes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Autoimmune destruction of the ovaries accompanies the thyroiditis

explanation.summary: Primary hypothyroidism raises TRH, which increases prolactin; hyperprolactinemia suppresses pulsatile GnRH and causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
explanation.whyCorrect: In primary hypothyroidism, reduced thyroid-hormone feedback increases hypothalamic TRH secretion. Increased TRH can raise prolactin secretion, and hyperprolactinemia may suppress pulsatile GnRH secretion, reducing LH and FSH and contributing to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, which fits her low estradiol with low gonadotropins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture describes no direct ovarian action of TSH; the pathway to hypogonadism runs through TRH, prolactin, and GnRH.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aromatase converts androgen precursors to estrogens in peripheral tissues; its inhibition is not the described consequence of hypothyroidism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gonadotrope desensitization results from continuous GnRH-receptor activation, as with GnRH-agonist therapy, not from elevated TSH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ovarian destruction would cause primary hypogonadism with elevated LH and FSH, but her gonadotropins are low.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism from hypothalamic dysfunction has used testosterone replacement for 3 years and has normal secondary sex characteristics. He and his partner now wish to conceive, and he asks about treatment to stimulate his testes. Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An increased dose of testosterone replacement

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pulsatile GnRH therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: A long-acting GnRH agonist

choices.label: D
choices.text: An aromatase inhibitor

choices.label: E
choices.text: A short course of low-dose estrogen

explanation.summary: Pulsatile GnRH or gonadotropin therapy is used in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism when gonadal stimulation or fertility is desired.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testosterone replacement maintains pubertal development but does not stimulate the testes. In selected patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who desire gonadal stimulation or fertility, pulsatile GnRH or gonadotropin therapy is used; pulsatile delivery mimics physiologic hypothalamic secretion and drives pituitary LH and FSH release to activate testicular steroidogenic and gametogenic function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: More testosterone maintains secondary sex characteristics but provides no gonadotropin signal to activate testicular gametogenic function.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Continuous exposure from a long-acting agonist desensitizes gonadotropes and suppresses LH and FSH, the opposite of the goal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aromatase inhibition blocks conversion of androgens to estrogens in peripheral tissues and does not restore the missing gonadotropin drive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estrogen is used to induce pubertal development in females with persistent hypogonadism; it has no role in stimulating this man's testes.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy has delayed puberty. A thorough history, physical examination, and diagnostic evaluation reveal no underlying pathology, and his father entered puberty late; constitutional delay of growth and puberty is diagnosed. The boy is deeply distressed about his appearance and is withdrawing socially. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A long-acting GnRH agonist

choices.label: B
choices.text: Growth hormone injections

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pulsatile GnRH infusion therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Long-term high-dose testosterone therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: A short course of low-dose testosterone

explanation.summary: In CDGP with substantial distress and no underlying pathology, a short course of low-dose testosterone may be used to initiate pubertal development.
explanation.whyCorrect: When pubertal delay causes substantial distress and no underlying pathology is identified, a short course of low-dose testosterone (or estrogen in females) may be considered to initiate pubertal development. Because CDGP progresses spontaneously, treatment is brief, individualized, and appropriately monitored.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A GnRH agonist suppresses gonadotropin secretion and is used to halt central precocious puberty, the opposite problem.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Growth hormone is not indicated; his delay is a variation in pubertal timing, not growth hormone deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pulsatile GnRH therapy is reserved for selected patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism when gonadal stimulation or fertility is desired, not for CDGP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CDGP culminates in spontaneous puberty, so prolonged high-dose androgen therapy is inappropriate; only a short low-dose course is considered.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old girl has no breast development and no other signs of puberty. Her physician suspects hypogonadism and wants first to determine whether the problem lies at the level of the gonads or at the level of the hypothalamus and pituitary. Which of the following sets of measurements is most useful for making this distinction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Serum LH, FSH, and estradiol concentrations

choices.label: B
choices.text: Serum DHEAS and androstenedione concentrations

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum growth hormone and IGF-1 concentrations

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum TSH and prolactin concentrations

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum hCG and progesterone concentrations

explanation.summary: LH, FSH, and the appropriate gonadal steroid distinguish primary from secondary hypogonadism.
explanation.whyCorrect: Primary hypogonadism produces low estradiol with elevated LH and FSH because loss of sex-steroid negative feedback increases gonadotropin secretion, whereas secondary hypogonadism produces low estradiol with low or inappropriately normal LH and FSH. Interpreting gonadotropins together with the gonadal steroid and the clinical findings localizes the level of dysfunction.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Adrenal androgen precursors reflect adrenarche and adrenal function; they do not localize HPG-axis dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GH and IGF-1 assess the growth axis, which does not distinguish gonadal from hypothalamic-pituitary causes of absent puberty.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TSH and prolactin screen for specific secondary causes such as hypothyroidism with hyperprolactinemia, but they do not by themselves classify hypogonadism as primary or secondary.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG relates to germ-cell tumors and luteal progesterone requires ovulation; neither measurement localizes the level of hypogonadism.

questions.stem: A physiology student asks what happens to hypothalamic GnRH secretion once puberty has been completed. Which of the following best describes GnRH secretion after pubertal activation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continuous secretion maintained at a constant rate throughout adulthood

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pulsatile secretion that persists only until epiphyseal fusion occurs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complete cessation once adult sex-steroid concentrations are reached

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pulsatile secretion whose frequency and amplitude vary with physiologic state

choices.label: E
choices.text: Continuous secretion with amplitude that increases steadily with age

explanation.summary: Pulsatile GnRH secretion continues after pubertal activation, with frequency and amplitude that vary by developmental stage and physiologic state.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pulsatile GnRH secretion continues after pubertal activation, with frequency and amplitude that vary according to developmental stage and physiologic state. Ongoing pulsatility is required, because continuous GnRH exposure desensitizes gonadotropes and suppresses LH and FSH secretion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Continuous GnRH exposure desensitizes pituitary gonadotropes and suppresses gonadotropin secretion, so constant secretion is not the physiologic pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH pulsatility is not tied to growth-plate closure; it continues to drive gonadal steroid production and gametogenic function after fusion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adult gonadal function depends on continued gonadotropin stimulation, which requires ongoing pulsatile GnRH rather than cessation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The physiologic pattern is pulsatile, not continuous, and its parameters vary with physiologic state rather than rising steadily with age.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has 3 months of pubic hair growth, penile enlargement, and accelerated linear growth. Both testes are prepubertal in size. Serum testosterone is elevated, LH and FSH are suppressed, hCG is undetectable, and adrenal androgen levels are not elevated. His father applies a topical testosterone gel daily, and the boy frequently naps on his father's bare chest. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: hCG-secreting germ-cell tumor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Central precocious puberty

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exogenous androgen exposure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Leydig-cell tumor

explanation.summary: Exogenous hormone exposure causes GnRH-independent precocious puberty with suppressed gonadotropins and, in boys, prepubertal testes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Exogenous hormone exposure is a cause of peripheral, GnRH-independent precocious puberty. Transferred testosterone virilizes the child and suppresses LH and FSH, and because there is neither gonadotropin drive nor an intratesticular source, both testes remain prepubertal; the close skin contact with a testosterone gel user identifies the exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An hCG-secreting tumor stimulates Leydig-cell testosterone production via LH receptors, but hCG is undetectable in this patient.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Central precocious puberty is gonadotropin-driven, so testicular enlargement would be present and LH and FSH would not be suppressed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia supplies adrenal androgens, but his adrenal androgen levels are not elevated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A Leydig-cell tumor produces testosterone within a testis, which would cause enlargement of the affected testis rather than bilaterally prepubertal testes.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old boy is brought in because his parents are worried that he is shorter than most of the girls in his class, several of whom have grown rapidly this year. His height is at the 50th percentile for age, his genital development is appropriate for age, and his examination is otherwise normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Initiation of growth hormone injections

choices.label: B
choices.text: A short course of low-dose testosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Karyotype analysis for a chromosomal disorder

choices.label: D
choices.text: Initiation of a long-acting GnRH agonist

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reassurance that growth and development are age-appropriate

explanation.summary: A boy with age-appropriate height and sexual development who lags behind female classmates reflects the later timing of the male growth spurt and needs only reassurance.
explanation.whyCorrect: The male pubertal growth spurt generally begins later than the female spurt, so girls of the same age may transiently be taller. Because his height is average for age and his sexual development is appropriate, there is no evidence of growth hormone deficiency or pubertal disorder, and no treatment is indicated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Growth hormone treatment is not indicated when there is no evidence of growth hormone deficiency and height is appropriate for age.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Low-dose testosterone is considered for distressing delayed puberty without underlying pathology; this boy's pubertal development is on time.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Karyotyping evaluates suspected gonadal dysgenesis or failure in delayed puberty; he has normal, age-appropriate development.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A GnRH agonist suppresses the HPG axis to halt precocious puberty and has no role in a normally developing boy.
